passages.heading: Overview and recommended steps
passages.text:
- Check the expiry date on your residence status in advance. A D-2 student who needs more time to study must apply for extension of stay before their authorized stay expires.
- Confirm continued enrollment and the university’s international office instructions. The immigration office can require additional evidence based on study progress and personal circumstances.
- Use the official Stay Extension guidance, then check HiKorea for online application eligibility or reservation. Do not assume an online option exists for every case.
- Prepare the application, passport, residence card, evidence of enrollment or ongoing study, evidence of residence, and any additional items specified for your D-2 subtype. Proof of finances, tuition payment, or academic progress may be required in individual cases.
- Submit the application through the permitted route before expiry, pay the assessed fee, and retain application/receipt information. Follow requests for supplemental evidence.
- Do not treat application submission as automatic approval; verify your status and any travel restrictions while an extension is pending.

passages.heading: 4. Extending period of stay (체류기간 연장)
passages.text:
A residence card is evidence of registered status. Its physical replacement is NOT the mechanism for permission to remain longer. A D-2 or D-4 student who needs to stay beyond the authorized expiry date must request extension of period of stay before expiry, with the evidence appropriate to the student and institution.

1. Check the authorized stay expiry date and current visa subtype; do not rely only on the plastic card’s appearance.
1. Ask the university international office whether it offers student-group extension or issues required enrollment, attendance and financial documents.
1. Check HiKorea for current eligibility for e-application or make a visit reservation.
1. Prepare passport, residence card, application form, fee, proof of enrollment and residence, and additional immigration-requested records.
1. Submit the application before the current permitted stay ends and follow any instructions for biometric/card updates or additional evidence.
Risk situations: taking leave of absence, withdrawing, graduating, changing universities, or ending a language program can affect the basis for student stay. Do not assume the printed expiry date guarantees permission after a change in academic status. Seek university and immigration advice promptly.

passages.heading: 2) Student (D-2)
passages.text:
Students must obtain a Student (D-2) visa to enroll in regular degree programs at
institutions of higher education in Korea, including associate, bachelor’s, master’s,
and doctoral degree programs.

Eligibility
Foreign nationals who intend to enroll in regular degree programs
or conduct specific research at the following educational institutions:

[Educational Institutions]

Universities or university-affiliated language institutes that meet
the requirements set by the Minister of Justice as educational
or research institutions being equivalent to or higher than junior
colleges established under the Higher Education Act or Special
Acts.

• (Exceptions) The following are excluded from educational
institutions attended by students eligible for the Student visa:
➀ Broadcasting universities, correspondence universities, open

universities, and cyber (online) universities as defined in
Article 2(5) of the Higher Education Act

➁ Lifelong education institutions as defined in Article 2(2) of the

Lifelong Education Act

19

➂ Vocational training programs among technical colleges as

defined in Article 2(5) of the National Lifelong Vocational Skills
Development Act

➃ Night colleges and graduate schools, excluding certain night

degree programs* eligible for student visas.
* Night graduate schools without daytime programs or night advanced

major programs at junior colleges that have undergone prior
screening for night degree programs by the competent immigration
office.

passages.heading: 2) Eligibility
passages.text:
Students with a certain level of Korean proficiency who are committed to their
primary purpose of study (language training) and who have obtained approval from
the university staff in charge of international students

• Students holding the following visa types among all student visas: D-2-1 through
D-2-4, D-2-6, and D-2-7

• Students whose visa status has changed from language training (D-4-1, D-4-7) or
visiting student (D-2-8) and who have stayed in Korea for more than six months
since the date of status change (or since the date of entry for visa holders)
※ Students who have completed the regular education program at a university but do not

meet the graduation requirements (i.e., grades, attendance rate) and who have been

exceptionally permitted to stay as a result are not eligible.

• Among those who have completed a master’s or a doctoral program, however,
students who have received a special visa extension for the purpose of thesis
preparation are exceptionally permitted to work. The permitted working hours are
up to 30 hours per week, and unlimited permission does not apply during days
off, public holidays, and vacation periods.

passages.heading: 5. Frequently asked questions (retrieval targets)
passages.text:
Q. Can I begin my university degree with a D-4 visa?

A. Check whether a D-2 status change is required and secure approval before commencing activities requiring D-2.

Q. Does a job offer convert my visa automatically?

A. No. Immigration approval is required for a change of status when applicable.

Q. Can everyone apply for D-10?

A. No. Eligibility and exclusions depend on individual history and criteria.

passages.heading: Overview and recommended steps
passages.text:
- Check the expiry date on your residence status in advance. A D-2 student who needs more time to study must apply for extension of stay before their authorized stay expires.

- Submit the application through the permitted route before expiry, pay the assessed fee, and retain application/receipt information. Follow requests for supplemental evidence.
- Do not treat application submission as automatic approval; verify your status and any travel restrictions while an extension is pending.

passages.heading: FAQ 3. I lost my ARC. Is reporting it online enough?
passages.text: No. HiKorea’s online loss report helps prevent misuse. You must separately follow the reissuance procedure for a replacement card.

passages.heading: Immediate action and replacement steps
passages.text:
1. If lost, use HiKorea → Information Inquiry (정보조회) → Report Lost Residence Card (등록증·거소증 분실(철회) 신고) to reduce misuse risk.
1. Check whether theft requires a police report for personal or insurance reasons; request assistance from the university or 1345 when needed.
1. Arrange a replacement-card (재발급) application through the appropriate immigration channel; a loss report by itself is not a new card.
1. Bring passport, integrated application form, photograph if requested, evidence of loss/damage if applicable, old card when damaged, and the current reissuance fee.
1. Keep submission evidence and confirm any travel, banking, or identity-verification needs with the relevant institution while the card is absent.
Timing caution: older official guidance specifies prompt reissuance after loss, including a 14-day requirement. Because the latest applicable rule and filing arrangements may change, verify the current deadline at HiKorea or immigration 1345 immediately rather than waiting.

If the card is found after reporting it lost, ask immigration how to withdraw the loss report and whether the original card remains usable. Do not assume it is automatically valid.

passages.heading: Overview and recommended steps
passages.text:
- Before departure, check your passport validity, residence-card validity, current authorized stay, and any pending visa/status application.
- The Ministry of Justice announced a re-entry permit exemption for many registered foreigners returning within one year; the exemption is limited by the remaining period of authorized stay and immigration exceptions. Confirm that the policy still applies to your status and travel dates.
- Do not assume an expired residence card or an extension application guarantees admission back into Korea.
- Ask immigration (1345) before international travel if your status is changing, renewal is pending, your residence card is lost, or you will be outside Korea for an extended period.
- Check the destination country’s entry/visa requirements, your airline’s document requirements, and any transit visa obligations.
- On return, carry passport, residence card where applicable, and evidence of student status if useful. Border officials make the final entry determination.

passages.heading: 7. Chatbot RAG retrieval and escalation policy
passages.text:
- Identify the question type FIRST: first_registration / lost_card / card_reissue / extension_of_stay / registration_change / address_change.
- Ask only for missing necessary details (visa type, entry date, expiry date, move date, card status or passport issuance date). Never request full passport number or ARC number in ordinary chat.
- Prefer Korean immigration official pages and exact service descriptions; cite the source URL and note when a rule was checked.
- For deadlines or penalties, return exact verified rule + exceptions, avoiding blanket advice across visa categories.
- When information is conflicting, outdated, or student status is complicated, advise contacting 1345 / immigration and optionally a university supporter; do not route the student to a supporter before attempting a grounded answer.
- Never say a student is approved, legal to remain, or exempt from reporting without evidence from the competent authority.

passages.heading: 5. Documents checklist
passages.text:
- Passport and/or valid Residence Card (ARC): the official Study in Korea checklist lists both. Bring both when available. [S1]
- Application or report form (체류지 변경신고서), if required by the office/channel. [S1, S2]
- Evidence of your new residence, selected for your housing arrangement. [S1, S2]

passages.heading: 4. Step-by-step: Online report
passages.text:
1. Prepare your residence card (ARC), passport details, the exact new address and proof of occupancy.
1. Open https://www.hikorea.go.kr/ and sign in using an available verification method.
1. Find the electronic civil service for reporting a change of place of stay (체류지 변경신고); menus can change over time.
1. Complete the requested move-in date and new address, upload supporting documents and submit.
1. Check the application result, save confirmation and verify that your registered address was updated. If the online service is unavailable or rejects the submission, use an eligible in-person reporting channel before the deadline.

passages.heading: Immediate action and replacement steps
passages.text:
1. If lost, use HiKorea → Information Inquiry (정보조회) → Report Lost Residence Card (등록증·거소증 분실(철회) 신고) to reduce misuse risk.
1. Check whether theft requires a police report for personal or insurance reasons; request assistance from the university or 1345 when needed.
1. Arrange a replacement-card (재발급) application through the appropriate immigration channel; a loss report by itself is not a new card.
1. Bring passport, integrated application form, photograph if requested, evidence of loss/damage if applicable, old card when damaged, and the current reissuance fee.
1. Keep submission evidence and confirm any travel, banking, or identity-verification needs with the relevant institution while the card is absent.
Timing caution: older official guidance specifies prompt reissuance after loss, including a 14-day requirement. Because the latest applicable rule and filing arrangements may change, verify the current deadline at HiKorea or immigration 1345 immediately rather than waiting.

If the card is found after reporting it lost, ask immigration how to withdraw the loss report and whether the original card remains usable. Do not assume it is automatically valid.

passages.heading: 1. Important rules at a glance
passages.text:
| Procedure | Key information |
| First foreigner registration | Generally within 90 days after entering Korea when intending to stay over 90 days. |
| Initial application | Use HiKorea visit reservation and apply at the immigration office with jurisdiction over residence; some universities coordinate group submissions. |
| Physical card fee | KRW 35,000 for issuance/reissuance since 1 January 2025; other immigration service fees can apply separately. |
| Lost card | Report loss on HiKorea to reduce misuse risk, then separately apply for reissuance promptly. |
| Stay renewal | Extend permitted period of stay BEFORE expiration; replacing the plastic card alone does not extend status. |
| Address change | Registered foreigners generally report their new residence within 15 days after moving. |
| Passport information | Report applicable changes; the passport-reporting deadline has special rules, so check the current HiKorea notice or 1345. |

Important distinction: “ARC renewal” is colloquial. Government immigration procedures distinguish extension of period of stay (체류기간 연장), reissuance of a residence card (등록증 재발급), and reporting changes to registration details (등록사항 변경신고).

passages.heading: 5. Changes to registered information (등록사항 변경신고)
passages.text:
Students must distinguish changes in identity/passport records from changes in their place of stay. The required channel, evidence and reporting deadline differ.

| Change | Deadline / distinction | Action |
| Moved to a different residence (체류지 변경신고) | Generally within 15 days after moving for registered foreign residents. | Report via eligible HiKorea e-service, local government office or immigration office; provide new proof of residence. |
| New passport / passport number (여권정보 변경신고) | Special passport-reporting rules apply; do not automatically use the address deadline. | Older official Visa Navigator guidance mentions 45 days after passport issuance and a receipt-date exception; verify current rule and accepted proof. |
| Name, nationality, sex, date of birth or other registration particulars (등록사항 변경신고) | A reporting obligation can apply, often within a short statutory period. | Check exact trigger, deadline and required documentary evidence with immigration before submitting. |
| Change of visa status (체류자격 변경허가) | Permission generally needed before activities of the new status. | This is a status application, not merely a card-details update. |

For address-change details, link this article to the separate RAG article “Change of Address in South Korea”.

passages.heading: 1) Foreigner Registration and Issuance of a Residence Card
passages.text:
Foreigners who plan to stay in Korea for 90 days or longer must register as foreign-
ers within 90 days of entry at the Immigration Office and obtain a residence card.
The residence card serves as an identification card, and it is used for various purposes
during one’s stay in Korea including using banking services, opening a mobile phone
account, and registering for health insurance. All foreigners staying in Korea must carry
their residence card at all times.
International students returning to their schools in Korea after a leave of absence must
register as foreigners within 90 days of entry and have their residence card reissued.

passages.heading: Application steps
passages.text:
1. Confirm the student’s visa status, arrival date, current address, and whether their university offers group registration.
1. Reserve an immigration visit through HiKorea (www.hikorea.go.kr), unless the university has an authorized group process.
1. Prepare the integrated application form, valid passport, recent passport-style photograph, and proof of residence.
1. Prepare a certificate of enrollment or training and any visa-specific documents required by immigration.
1. Attend the appointment, submit the application, complete required biometric procedures if applicable, pay the applicable fees, and follow the collection/delivery instructions.

passages.heading: Overview and recommended steps
passages.text:
- Before departure, check your passport validity, residence-card validity, current authorized stay, and any pending visa/status application.
- The Ministry of Justice announced a re-entry permit exemption for many registered foreigners returning within one year; the exemption is limited by the remaining period of authorized stay and immigration exceptions. Confirm that the policy still applies to your status and travel dates.
- Do not assume an expired residence card or an extension application guarantees admission back into Korea.
- Ask immigration (1345) before international travel if your status is changing, renewal is pending, your residence card is lost, or you will be outside Korea for an extended period.
- Check the destination country’s entry/visa requirements, your airline’s document requirements, and any transit visa obligations.

passages.heading: 5. Changes to registered information (등록사항 변경신고)
passages.text:
Students must distinguish changes in identity/passport records from changes in their place of stay. The required channel, evidence and reporting deadline differ.

| Change | Deadline / distinction | Action |
| Moved to a different residence (체류지 변경신고) | Generally within 15 days after moving for registered foreign residents. | Report via eligible HiKorea e-service, local government office or immigration office; provide new proof of residence. |
| New passport / passport number (여권정보 변경신고) | Special passport-reporting rules apply; do not automatically use the address deadline. | Older official Visa Navigator guidance mentions 45 days after passport issuance and a receipt-date exception; verify current rule and accepted proof. |
| Name, nationality, sex, date of birth or other registration particulars (등록사항 변경신고) | A reporting obligation can apply, often within a short statutory period. | Check exact trigger, deadline and required documentary evidence with immigration before submitting. |
| Change of visa status (체류자격 변경허가) | Permission generally needed before activities of the new status. | This is a status application, not merely a card-details update. |

For address-change details, link this article to the separate RAG article “Change of Address in South Korea”.

passages.heading: 1. Important rules at a glance
passages.text:
| Procedure | Key information |
| First foreigner registration | Generally within 90 days after entering Korea when intending to stay over 90 days. |
| Initial application | Use HiKorea visit reservation and apply at the immigration office with jurisdiction over residence; some universities coordinate group submissions. |
| Physical card fee | KRW 35,000 for issuance/reissuance since 1 January 2025; other immigration service fees can apply separately. |
| Lost card | Report loss on HiKorea to reduce misuse risk, then separately apply for reissuance promptly. |
| Stay renewal | Extend permitted period of stay BEFORE expiration; replacing the plastic card alone does not extend status. |
| Address change | Registered foreigners generally report their new residence within 15 days after moving. |
| Passport information | Report applicable changes; the passport-reporting deadline has special rules, so check the current HiKorea notice or 1345. |

Important distinction: “ARC renewal” is colloquial. Government immigration procedures distinguish extension of period of stay (체류기간 연장), reissuance of a residence card (등록증 재발급), and reporting changes to registration details (등록사항 변경신고).

passages.heading: Overview and recommended steps
passages.text:
- Before departure, check your passport validity, residence-card validity, current authorized stay, and any pending visa/status application.
- The Ministry of Justice announced a re-entry permit exemption for many registered foreigners returning within one year; the exemption is limited by the remaining period of authorized stay and immigration exceptions. Confirm that the policy still applies to your status and travel dates.
- Do not assume an expired residence card or an extension application guarantees admission back into Korea.
- Ask immigration (1345) before international travel if your status is changing, renewal is pending, your residence card is lost, or you will be outside Korea for an extended period.
- Check the destination country’s entry/visa requirements, your airline’s document requirements, and any transit visa obligations.
- On return, carry passport, residence card where applicable, and evidence of student status if useful. Border officials make the final entry determination.

passages.heading: 1) Foreigner Registration and Issuance of a Residence Card
passages.text:
Foreigners who plan to stay in Korea for 90 days or longer must register as foreign-
ers within 90 days of entry at the Immigration Office and obtain a residence card.
The residence card serves as an identification card, and it is used for various purposes
during one’s stay in Korea including using banking services, opening a mobile phone
account, and registering for health insurance. All foreigners staying in Korea must carry
their residence card at all times.
International students returning to their schools in Korea after a leave of absence must
register as foreigners within 90 days of entry and have their residence card reissued.

passages.heading: Immediate action and replacement steps
passages.text:
1. If lost, use HiKorea → Information Inquiry (정보조회) → Report Lost Residence Card (등록증·거소증 분실(철회) 신고) to reduce misuse risk.
1. Check whether theft requires a police report for personal or insurance reasons; request assistance from the university or 1345 when needed.
1. Arrange a replacement-card (재발급) application through the appropriate immigration channel; a loss report by itself is not a new card.
1. Bring passport, integrated application form, photograph if requested, evidence of loss/damage if applicable, old card when damaged, and the current reissuance fee.
1. Keep submission evidence and confirm any travel, banking, or identity-verification needs with the relevant institution while the card is absent.
Timing caution: older official guidance specifies prompt reissuance after loss, including a 14-day requirement. Because the latest applicable rule and filing arrangements may change, verify the current deadline at HiKorea or immigration 1345 immediately rather than waiting.

If the card is found after reporting it lost, ask immigration how to withdraw the loss report and whether the original card remains usable. Do not assume it is automatically valid.

Registered foreigners, including most D-2 and D-4 international students with residence registration, must report a change of their place of stay within 15 days of moving to the new address. passages.text: Ask for visa subtype, degree program, school year, language qualification, academic/institutional eligibility, semester versus vacation, and permit details before answering.

passages.heading: 2) Eligibility
passages.text:
Students with a certain level of Korean proficiency who are committed to their
primary purpose of study (language training) and who have obtained approval from
the university staff in charge of international students

• Students holding the following visa types among all student visas: D-2-1 through
D-2-4, D-2-6, and D-2-7

• Students whose visa status has changed from language training (D-4-1, D-4-7) or
visiting student (D-2-8) and who have stayed in Korea for more than six months
since the date of status change (or since the date of entry for visa holders)
※ Students who have completed the regular education program at a university but do not

meet the graduation requirements (i.e., grades, attendance rate) and who have been

exceptionally permitted to stay as a result are not eligible.

• Among those who have completed a master’s or a doctoral program, however,
students who have received a special visa extension for the purpose of thesis
preparation are exceptionally permitted to work. The permitted working hours are
up to 30 hours per week, and unlimited permission does not apply during days
off, public holidays, and vacation periods.

passages.heading: 1. Core answer: How do I legally start a part-time job?
passages.text:
1. Find an employer willing to hire an eligible international student; confirm the job category is allowed.
1. Sign a standard employment contract (근로계약서) specifying hourly wage, duties, location, hours and dates.
1. Complete the Part-Time Employment Confirmation Form (외국인 유학생 시간제취업 확인서) with confirmation/signature from the university international-student advisor.
1. Submit the application and supporting documents through HiKorea (when the relevant online service is available) or at the immigration office.
1. Receive approval (online printable permission or an approval sticker, as applicable) BEFORE starting work. Work only within the permitted conditions.
Official source: Study in Korea, “Part-Time Work for International Students,” section Approval Process [S1].

passages.heading: 4. Working hours and language proficiency
passages.text:
The official Study in Korea page distinguishes a basic limit from enhanced limits based on proficiency and institutional/academic conditions. The table below summarizes published categories, NOT automatic authorization. Exact permitted hours must match the student’s actual approval. [S1, S2]

| Program | Typical proficiency benchmark | If benchmark not met | If benchmark met / qualifying conditions |
| D-4 language training | TOPIK 2 or accepted equivalent | 10 hours | 20 hours; up to 25 under specified advantages |
| Associate degree | TOPIK 3 or accepted equivalent | 10 hours | 25 weekday hours; higher qualified allowance up to 30 |
| Bachelor years 1–2 | TOPIK 3 or accepted equivalent | 10 hours | 25 weekday hours; higher qualified allowance up to 30 |
| Bachelor years 3–4 | TOPIK 4 or accepted equivalent | 10 hours | 25 weekday hours; higher qualified allowance up to 30 |
| Master / doctorate | TOPIK 4 or accepted equivalent | 15 hours | 30 weekday hours; higher qualified allowance up to 35 |

Important weekend/holiday warning: The source shows unlimited weekends/vacations for some qualifying degree students, but NOT all students. Some categories have restricted weekend hours, and students with special post-course extensions can lose exemptions. Never promise “unlimited work” without confirming individual status and permit terms. [S1, S2]

passages.heading: 2) Eligibility
passages.text:
Students with a certain level of Korean proficiency who are committed to their
primary purpose of study (language training) and who have obtained approval from
the university staff in charge of international students

• Students holding the following visa types among all student visas: D-2-1 through
D-2-4, D-2-6, and D-2-7

• Students whose visa status has changed from language training (D-4-1, D-4-7) or
visiting student (D-2-8) and who have stayed in Korea for more than six months
since the date of status change (or since the date of entry for visa holders)
※ Students who have completed the regular education program at a university but do not

meet the graduation requirements (i.e., grades, attendance rate) and who have been

exceptionally permitted to stay as a result are not eligible.

• Among those who have completed a master’s or a doctoral program, however,
students who have received a special visa extension for the purpose of thesis
preparation are exceptionally permitted to work. The permitted working hours are
up to 30 hours per week, and unlimited permission does not apply during days
off, public holidays, and vacation periods.

passages.heading: Job Preparation Process
passages.text:
International students can begin job seeking after converting their student visa to a job-seeking visa.

Internship opportunities in Korea are available for up to 6 months, and students can transition from short-term internships to long-term employment after graduation.

Long-term employment is also possible immediately after graduation. Be sure to check the Korean Language Proficiency Recognition Criteria before applying for jobs.

passages.heading: 8. Chatbot answer policy and escalation
passages.text:
- Answer the deadline first: report within 15 days of the actual move-in date. Cite official national sources. [S1]
- If documents are unclear, ask for the accommodation type (dormitory, lease, living with another person) rather than asking for a full address or ID number in chat.
- Do not collect or reproduce passport numbers, ARC numbers, copies of IDs, rental contracts or students’ precise home addresses in chatbot conversations.
- Escalate cases involving missed deadlines, conflicting residence evidence, pending first registration, disputed occupancy or system errors to immigration (1345) first. University supporter referral may help with interpretation and steps, but must not replace an official legal decision.
- For uncertain online navigation, link to the HiKorea homepage rather than inventing a direct form path.

passages.heading: 8. Chatbot decision rules and escalation
passages.text:
Minimum facts to collect only when necessary: (1) visa category/subtype; (2) language trainee, associate, bachelor year, or graduate; (3) TOPIK / equivalent; (4) proposed work duties; (5) proposed weekly schedule and semester/vacation; (6) whether university confirmation and immigration permission have already been obtained.

- First retrieve official passages and answer the user’s immediate question, with source citation and last-checked date.
- Do not infer authorization from a TOPIK level alone; never guarantee a specific hour limit or workplace category without permit verification.
- If a case involves visa exceptions, special course status, unlisted jobs, multiple workplaces, or conflicting rules, instruct the student to confirm with the university or call 1345. Offer supporter handoff only if unresolved.
- Protect privacy: do not request passport numbers, ARC numbers, employer IDs, or scans in the public chatbot.

passages.heading: Q: Do I need to report if I move to another city?
passages.text: A: Yes. A registered foreign resident must report a changed place of stay, using the competent office for the new address. [S1]

passages.heading: In-person report
passages.text:
1. Go to the community service center for the new address or an appropriate immigration office.
1. Bring residence identification and documents proving the new accommodation.
1. Complete the change-of-place-of-stay report/application if required.
1. Request confirmation of processing and retain it for your records.

passages.heading: FAQ 5. I moved to a new dormitory. Do I need to notify immigration?
passages.text: An actual change of registered place of stay generally must be reported within 15 days, even if you stay within the same university area. Verify whether a room-only change altered the registered address.

최근 법무부 및 출입국·외국인청에서 외국인 유학생 대상 불법취업(무단 아르바이트) 집중 단속 및 조사를 실시하고 있습니다.

특히 SNS, 오픈채팅 및 외국인 대상 구인 어플리케이션 등을 통한 불법 근로 연계 사례가 다수 확인되고 있으며, 실제 출입국사무소 조사 및 출석 요구 사례도 발생하고 있습니다.

최근에는 외국인 구인 플랫폼인 Face One 등을 통해 단기·일용성 아르바이트를 연결받아 적발되는 사례가 증가하고 있으니 각별히 주의하시기 바랍니다.

1. 불법취업 해당 사례

- 시간제취업 허가 없이 근로 진행
- 허가받은 근무시간 초과 근로

- 허가받지 않은 업종·사업장 근무

- Face One 등 외국인 대상 구인 어플을 통한 단기 아르바이트 참여

- 현금 지급 형태의 무신고 근로

- 행사 보조, 통역, 판매, 홍보, 물류 업무 등 일용성 단기 근로

- SNS·오픈채팅을 통한 아르바이트 참여

※ “하루만”, “단기”, “현금 지급”, “외국인 가능” 형태의 모집도 모두 단속 대상이 될 수 있습니다.

- SNS·오픈채팅을 통한 아르바이트 참여

※ “하루만”, “단기”, “현금 지급”, “외국인 가능” 형태의 모집도 모두 단속 대상이 될 수 있습니다.

2. 적발 시 불이익

- 범칙금 부과

- 출입국사무소 출석 및 조사

- 시간제취업 허가 제한

- 체류기간 연장 제한

- 비자 변경 및 체류 심사 불이익

- 강제퇴거(추방) 조치

※ 위반 기간 및 횟수에 따라 범칙금이 크게 증가할 수 있으며, 중대한 위반으로 판단될 경우 강제퇴거 대상이 될 수 있습니다.

<불법취업 기간별 주요 범칙금 사례>

- 1개월 이상 : 약 300만원 수준 범칙금 부과 가능

- 6개월 이상 : 약 700만원 수준 범칙금 부과 가능

- 장기·반복 위반 : 강제퇴거 대상 포함 가능

3. 유의사항

최근 “단기 알바”, “하루 일당”, “통역 가능자 모집”, “외국인 가능” 등의 형태로 불법 근로 모집 사례가 증가하고 있습니다.

“다른 학생들도 하고 있다”, “잠깐만 도와주는 것이다”, “현금 지급이라 문제없다” 등의 안내를 받더라도, 적발 시 모든 책임은 본인에게 있습니다.

passages.text: No. Wait for an approval decision before undertaking the proposed work.

passages.heading: Wages and Working Conditions for Foreign Workers
passages.text:
- **1 Prohibition of Discrimination Against Foreign Workers** Employers shall not treat foreign workers unfairly due to their status as foreign workers.(Article 22 of the Act on the Employment of Foreign Workers, etc.).
- **2 Preparation of Standard Employment Contracts** Employers must use a standard employment contract when hiring foreign workers.(Regulation Article 9, Paragraph 1 of the Act on the Employment of Foreign Workers, etc.)

Violations may result in a fine of up to 5 million KRW. (Article 32, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph 1 of the Act on the Employment of Foreign Workers, etc.)
- **3 Direct, Full, and Regular Payment of Wages** Wages must be paid directly, in full, and on a regular basis at least once a month on a fixed date, in cash. (Article 43 of the Labor Standards Act)

Violations of this regulation may result in imprisonment for up to 3 years or a fine of up to 30 million KRW. Prosecution cannot be initiated against the explicit will of the victim in such
cases. (Article 109 of the Labor Standards Act)
- **4 Payment of Wages Above Minimum Wage** The wage levels of foreign workers do not necessarily need to match those of domestic workers and may vary based on experience and productivity.

Source : National Law Information Center | Booklet>Employment of Foreign Workers

passages.heading: 5. Types of work
passages.text:
- Ordinary student-type part-time work may include restaurant assistance, general office assistance, tourism-related support, and retail/duty-free sales assistance, subject to individual approval. [S2]
- Special professional activities and private tutoring may follow other rules; private tutoring is especially restricted. [S1]
- Do NOT assume delivery work, platform/gig work, construction work, freelance work, or work at a second workplace is allowed. Ask the immigration office before committing.
- Changing employer, worksite, role, or schedule can affect authorization. Check reporting or new-permit requirements before changing anything.

passages.heading: 8. Chatbot decision rules and escalation
passages.text:
Minimum facts to collect only when necessary: (1) visa category/subtype; (2) language trainee, associate, bachelor year, or graduate; (3) TOPIK / equivalent; (4) proposed work duties; (5) proposed weekly schedule and semester/vacation; (6) whether university confirmation and immigration permission have already been obtained.

- First retrieve official passages and answer the user’s immediate question, with source citation and last-checked date.
- Do not infer authorization from a TOPIK level alone; never guarantee a specific hour limit or workplace category without permit verification.
- If a case involves visa exceptions, special course status, unlisted jobs, multiple workplaces, or conflicting rules, instruct the student to confirm with the university or call 1345. Offer supporter handoff only if unresolved.
- Protect privacy: do not request passport numbers, ARC numbers, employer IDs, or scans in the public chatbot.

passages.heading: 1) National Health Insurance (NHI)
passages.text:
All international students staying in Korea for six months or longer are automatically
enrolled in the insurance as local subscribers* to NHI, receiving the same insurance
benefits as Korean nationals.
* Persons who register individually rather than as company employees

NHI Registration Process

Enter Korea
Register as a foreign
resident (must register
within 90 days of entry)

Automatic enrollment in
NHI (no separate application

required)

Pay a monthly health

insurance premium
The National Health Insurance Service

(NHIS) sends a notification letter
regarding registration and payment

※ Healthcare costs may be covered through a private health insurance plan until foreign resi-

dent registration is completed after entering Korea.

National Health Insurance Premiums Calculation

The NHI premium for international students is calculated un-
der the same standards applied to local Korean subscribers,
considering each student as a single household. However,
students holding a residency status eligible for abatement
[i.e., Student (D-2), General Trainee (D-4)] and whose
monthly income and assets are below the standards set by
NHI may receive a 50% discount on the monthly premium.

NHI Information for

Foreigners

※ Short-term visitors who stay in Korea for up to six months (e.g., exchange students, trainees)

are not eligible for automatic enrollment in NHI. However, some schools require international
students to register for a private health insurance plan or a group insurance plan, so please
check in advance.

※ Failure to pay the NHI premium will result in loss of coverage and higher medical expenses.

Please note that this may also affect visa extension eligibility.

passages.heading: 2. Rules and eligibility
passages.text:
- NHIS states D-2 students generally enroll from initial entry/foreigner registration as applicable; some D-4 categories may have a waiting period. Confirm exact enrollment date for the visa subtype.
- NHIS invoices may be delivered to the registered Korean address; maintain correct registration details.
- Insurance coverage does not mean every treatment or service is free; co-payments and exclusions can apply.
- Special premium reductions, financial hardship measures and exclusion for qualifying alternative coverage require case-specific NHIS confirmation.

passages.heading: 1) National Health Insurance (NHI)
passages.text:
All international students staying in Korea for six months or longer are automatically
enrolled in the insurance as local subscribers* to NHI, receiving the same insurance
benefits as Korean nationals.
* Persons who register individually rather than as company employees

NHI Registration Process

Enter Korea
Register as a foreign
resident (must register
within 90 days of entry)

Automatic enrollment in
NHI (no separate application

required)

Pay a monthly health

insurance premium
The National Health Insurance Service

(NHIS) sends a notification letter
regarding registration and payment

※ Healthcare costs may be covered through a private health insurance plan until foreign resi-

dent registration is completed after entering Korea.

National Health Insurance Premiums Calculation

The NHI premium for international students is calculated un-
der the same standards applied to local Korean subscribers,
considering each student as a single household. However,
students holding a residency status eligible for abatement
[i.e., Student (D-2), General Trainee (D-4)] and whose
monthly income and assets are below the standards set by
NHI may receive a 50% discount on the monthly premium.

NHI Information for

Foreigners

※ Short-term visitors who stay in Korea for up to six months (e.g., exchange students, trainees)

are not eligible for automatic enrollment in NHI. However, some schools require international
students to register for a private health insurance plan or a group insurance plan, so please
check in advance.

※ Failure to pay the NHI premium will result in loss of coverage and higher medical expenses.

Please note that this may also affect visa extension eligibility.

passages.heading: 3) Visiting Healthcare Providers
passages.text:
Mandatory ID check

Pursuant to the National Health Insurance Act, individuals visiting a healthcare
provider must verify their identity by presenting a valid ID card before receiving
medical services. Medical services cannot be provided without presenting an ID
card. Acceptable forms of identification include those with a photo and a foreign
resident registration number, such as a residence card, passport,
or driver's license issued in Korea. A mobile health insurance
card can also be used in place of a physical ID card.

passages.heading: Overview and recommended steps
passages.text:
- For life-threatening illness, injury, or loss of consciousness, call 119 immediately.
- For routine care, locate a clinic (의원) or hospital (병원) appropriate to symptoms, confirm opening hours and appointment requirements, and ask about availability of interpretation when necessary.
- Bring identification, your residence card or passport, and insurance information. Clinics and hospitals may verify NHIS eligibility through identity checks.
- NHIS gives official guidance on foreigner enrollment and exclusions, including circumstances involving qualifying alternative coverage. Verify your own coverage and payment status directly with NHIS.
- Ask the provider what portion of treatment and prescriptions is covered, what must be paid personally, and whether referrals are needed for certain hospital services.
- Keep prescriptions, visit receipts, and medical certificates if needed for university absence or insurer claims. For coverage or eligibility issues, contact NHIS foreign resident service channels.

passages.heading: 3) Visiting Healthcare Providers
passages.text:
Mandatory ID check

Pursuant to the National Health Insurance Act, individuals visiting a healthcare
provider must verify their identity by presenting a valid ID card before receiving
medical services. Medical services cannot be provided without presenting an ID
card. Acceptable forms of identification include those with a photo and a foreign
resident registration number, such as a residence card, passport,
or driver's license issued in Korea. A mobile health insurance
card can also be used in place of a physical ID card.

passages.heading: Overview and recommended steps
passages.text:
- For life-threatening illness, injury, or loss of consciousness, call 119 immediately.
- For routine care, locate a clinic (의원) or hospital (병원) appropriate to symptoms, confirm opening hours and appointment requirements, and ask about availability of interpretation when necessary.
- Bring identification, your residence card or passport, and insurance information. Clinics and hospitals may verify NHIS eligibility through identity checks.
- NHIS gives official guidance on foreigner enrollment and exclusions, including circumstances involving qualifying alternative coverage. Verify your own coverage and payment status directly with NHIS.
- Ask the provider what portion of treatment and prescriptions is covered, what must be paid personally, and whether referrals are needed for certain hospital services.
- Keep prescriptions, visit receipts, and medical certificates if needed for university absence or insurer claims. For coverage or eligibility issues, contact NHIS foreign resident service channels.

passages.heading: (3) Language Proficiency Requirements
passages.text:
Students may apply for the Korean Language Program without submitting any
language proficiency documents. However, when applying for degree programs,
applicants must submit official Korean or English proficiency test scores that meet
the minimum requirements set by the university (or department) they wish to apply
to.

English Proficiency Requirements

Universities usually accept TOEFL, IELTS, and TEPS scores as official English
proficiency tests.
However, applicants should check the admission guidelines of the university (or
department) where they wish to apply, as different universities may require specific
tests or score thresholds.

8

Korean Proficiency Requirements

- Test of Proficiency in Korean (TOPIK)
TOPIK is an official test used to assess Korean language proficiency among foreign
nationals and overseas Koreans whose first language is not Korean. Test results are
used for various purposes including admission to Korean universities, scholarship
applications, job hunting, and visa issuance.

Test Overview

✓ Administering Organization:

National Institute for International Education (NIIED)

✓ Test Schedule(Based in Korea)

• Paper-Based Test (PBT, conducted six times a year):
January, April, May, July, October, and November
• Internet-Based Test (IBT, conducted six times a year):
February, March, June, September, October, and November
• TOPIK Speaking (three times a year): March, June, and October
※ Please check the overseas test schedule with the administering agency in your

country.

✓ How to Register for the Test: Register online at www.topik.go.kr

✓ Score Validity Period: Valid for two years from the date of result

announcement.

✓ Test Type and Level System

• TOPIK Paper-Based Test (PBT): TOPIK that is conducted in paper-based
format. The test consists of TOPIK I (Reading and Writing) and TOPIK II
(Listening, Reading, and Writing).

passages.heading: (2) Understanding Programs
passages.text:
✓ TOPIK Preparation Course: An intensive program designed to prepare

students for the TOPIK exam. It focuses on problem-solving practice
using actual past test questions.

✓ College Admission Course: Customized curriculum for Korean university

admission. Includes vocabulary commonly used in university majors.

✓ Short-term Intensive Course: A two- to four-week program offered

during vacation periods. It focuses on basic conversation and Korean
cultural experiences.

Degree Programs

Degree programs in Korea are divided into associate, bachelor's, master's, and
doctoral degrees. International applicants who meet the admission requirements
may submit application through the special admission track for international
students.

Programs are offered in either Korean or English depending on the university and
field of study. Once admitted, students must obtain a Student (D-2) Visa.

passages.heading: FAQ 5. I moved to a new dormitory. Do I need to notify immigration?
passages.text: An actual change of registered place of stay generally must be reported within 15 days, even if you stay within the same university area. Verify whether a room-only change altered the registered address.

passages.heading: 3. Application or response procedure
passages.text:
1. Identify current visa code, target visa code and planned activity start date.
1. Check current eligibility and document checklist with HiKorea and university/employer sponsor.
1. Gather application, passport, Residence Card and target-status-specific documents.
1. Submit through immigration using the eligible online or in-person channel and pay any fee.
1. Wait for permission before taking up status-restricted work or study activities.

passages.heading: Overview and recommended steps
passages.text:
- Check the expiry date on your residence status in advance. A D-2 student who needs more time to study must apply for extension of stay before their authorized stay expires.
- Confirm continued enrollment and the university’s international office instructions. The immigration office can require additional evidence based on study progress and personal circumstances.
- Use the official Stay Extension guidance, then check HiKorea for online application eligibility or reservation. Do not assume an online option exists for every case.
- Prepare the application, passport, residence card, evidence of enrollment or ongoing study, evidence of residence, and any additional items specified for your D-2 subtype. Proof of finances, tuition payment, or academic progress may be required in individual cases.
- Submit the application through the permitted route before expiry, pay the assessed fee, and retain application/receipt information. Follow requests for supplemental evidence.
- Do not treat application submission as automatic approval; verify your status and any travel restrictions while an extension is pending.

passages.heading: Approval Process
passages.text:
- **Step 1. Prepare an Employment Contract** Employment contract between the parties (standard employment contract, hourly wage must be stated).
- **Step 2. Prepare a Part-Time Employment Confirmation Form** Complete the designated form, signed by the university’s international student advisor.
- **Step 3. Application Submission** Submit required documents either online or in person.
- **Step 4. Approval or Rejection** Receive an approval sticker or print the permit online.

강신청 부정행위(해킹, 임의 삭제 등)에 따른 피해 방지 요망

확인기간에도 학과의 사정으로 시간표가 변경되는 경우가 있으니 수시 확인 필요

양, 전공기초 등)은 수강 가능하며 성적 취득 시 성적 산정 근거가 엄격히 관리됨

passages.heading: Overview and recommended steps
passages.text:
- Before departure, check your passport validity, residence-card validity, current authorized stay, and any pending visa/status application.
- The Ministry of Justice announced a re-entry permit exemption for many registered foreigners returning within one year; the exemption is limited by the remaining period of authorized stay and immigration exceptions. Confirm that the policy still applies to your status and travel dates.
- Do not assume an expired residence card or an extension application guarantees admission back into Korea.
- Ask immigration (1345) before international travel if your status is changing, renewal is pending, your residence card is lost, or you will be outside Korea for an extended period.
- Check the destination country’s entry/visa requirements, your airline’s document requirements, and any transit visa obligations.
- On return, carry passport, residence card where applicable, and evidence of student status if useful. Border officials make the final entry determination.

passages.heading: Job Opportunities and Position Types
passages.text:
There are numerous opportunities for international students to find employment in various fields.

Depending on their major, nationality, and language skills, international students can find diverse jobs and roles. It is recommended to seek positions related to their major and practical
experiences.

- ### Language Teacher Responsible for teaching foreign languages such as Korean, English, Chinese, etc.
- ### Interpreter and Translator Handles multilingual translation tasks.
- ### Trade and Tourism Roles Provides tourism information and guidance services for foreign tourists.
- ### Automotive, Shipbuilding, Aviation, and Railway Engineering Specialist Researches, designs, and consults on engines used in automobiles, ships, airplanes, and railways, as well as supervises, controls, and advises on their manufacturing and operation.
- ### Medical Coordinator Provides comprehensive services for foreign patients, including guidance and support for medical visits,

appointment scheduling, interpretation, and customer management.
- ### IT Sector Roles Handles roles such as software development, system operation, and network management in the IT field.
- ### Design Field Handles various design tasks such as UI/UX, web design, advertising, graphic design, and fashion design.
- ### Marketing Tasks Responsible for tasks such as multilingual content creation, exploring overseas markets, customer support, and marketing promotions.
- ### Academic Research Field Handles positions such as research assistant, teaching assistant, or researcher at universities and companies.
- ### HR, Accounting, and Management Fields Handles HR, accounting, and management roles within companies.

passages.heading: Overview and recommended steps
passages.text:
- Before departure, check your passport validity, residence-card validity, current authorized stay, and any pending visa/status application.
- The Ministry of Justice announced a re-entry permit exemption for many registered foreigners returning within one year; the exemption is limited by the remaining period of authorized stay and immigration exceptions. Confirm that the policy still applies to your status and travel dates.
- Do not assume an expired residence card or an extension application guarantees admission back into Korea.
- Ask immigration (1345) before international travel if your status is changing, renewal is pending, your residence card is lost, or you will be outside Korea for an extended period.
- Check the destination country’s entry/visa requirements, your airline’s document requirements, and any transit visa obligations.
- On return, carry passport, residence card where applicable, and evidence of student status if useful. Border officials make the final entry determination.

passages.heading: 2. Rules and eligibility
passages.text:
- Apply for change of stay status before engaging in activity that requires the new status.
- Changing from D-4 language training to D-2 study or D-2 graduation to D-10/E-series employment is not automatic.
- Application feasibility and supporting evidence depend on current visa subtype, destination visa subtype, academic achievements and immigration history.
- A university acceptance or employer offer is not the same as status-change approval.

passages.heading: Overview and recommended steps
passages.text:
- Check the expiry date on your residence status in advance. A D-2 student who needs more time to study must apply for extension of stay before their authorized stay expires.
- Confirm continued enrollment and the university’s international office instructions. The immigration office can require additional evidence based on study progress and personal circumstances.
- Use the official Stay Extension guidance, then check HiKorea for online application eligibility or reservation. Do not assume an online option exists for every case.
- Prepare the application, passport, residence card, evidence of enrollment or ongoing study, evidence of residence, and any additional items specified for your D-2 subtype. Proof of finances, tuition payment, or academic progress may be required in individual cases.
- Submit the application through the permitted route before expiry, pay the assessed fee, and retain application/receipt information. Follow requests for supplemental evidence.
- Do not treat application submission as automatic approval; verify your status and any travel restrictions while an extension is pending.

passages.heading: 1. Key answer
passages.text:
Registered foreigners, including most D-2 and D-4 international students with residence registration, must report a change of their place of stay within 15 days of moving to the new address. This requirement applies even when moving between dormitory rooms or from a dormitory to off-campus housing if the registered residential address changes. Reporting late may result in an administrative fine, which can be up to KRW 1,000,000. [S1]

Use the actual address where you live. The immigration address-change report is separate from changing a mailing address at a bank, school, telephone provider or delivery app.

Scholarships

There are various scholarship programs designed to support international students
in maintaining a stable academic life in Korea.

University Scholarships
Many universities offer a wide range of scholarships for international students.
In general, these scholarships cover 30 – 100% of tuition fees depending on
the student’s academic performance or Korean language proficiency.
Check the respective school websites or the Study in Korea website (http://

passages.heading: Essential Guide to Saving Living Expenses
passages.text:
The goal of studying abroad is not just to earn a degree but to grow through diverse experiences, making it important to save costs while having meaningful time.

- **Use Scholarships** The Korea government provides scholarships to international students annually, and students with excellent academic performance can receive university-specific scholarships.
- **Save on Housing Costs** Staying in dormitories or sharing an apartment with roommates can help reduce housing expenses.
- **Save on Food Expenses** Cook meals using groceries instead of dining out and take advantage of student discounts.
- **Save on Transportation Costs** Many cities in Korea offer bicycle rental services. Using Korea's affordable public transportation system with transfer benefits can also help save money.

passages.heading: Korea's Education System
passages.text:
Korea’s higher education system consists of bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degree programs offered by universities and vocational colleges,

as well as university-affiliated Korean language training programs.

passages.heading: Korea’s Education Structure
passages.text:
The Korean education system consists of a 16-year curriculum: 6 years of primary education, 6 years of secondary education (3 years of middle school, 3 years of high school).

Higher education institutions that international students can attend include 4-year universities, 2- to 3-year associate degree programs, and graduate schools offering master’s and doctoral
programs lasting 2 years or more.

passages.heading: (2) Understanding Programs
passages.text:
Korean Language Program

The Korean Language Program is an intensive course designed to help international
students improve their Korean language skills, which are essential for pursuing
degree programs or for daily life in Korea.
The program is generally offered by university-affiliated Korean language institutes,
and students are required to obtain a Korean Language Trainee (D-4-1) Visa.

6

University-Affiliated Korean Language Institutes
The institutes offer structured programs in speaking, listening, reading, and
writing to meet various needs such as university admission, job hunting, TOPIK
preparation, and business communication.

- Program Overview (Example)

※ Course details may vary depending on the language institute, so please check the

website of your chosen institute for the most accurate information.

<Regular Courses>
✓ Operation Period: Four semesters per year (Spring, Summer, Fall, Winter)

10 weeks per semester (within 200 Hours), 5 days a week (Monday–
Friday)

✓ Levels: Stage 1 (Beginner) – Stage 6 (Advanced). Students are placed by

their language proficiency.

✓ Course Structure: Listening, speaking, reading, and writing

✓ Evaluation Method: Based on attendance, tests, and homework

assignments.

✓ Completion Requirements: Students will receive a certificate of

completion upon meeting the required attendance and grade standards.
They may then advance to higher-level classes.

<Special or Short-term Courses>
In addition to regular courses, the institutes also offer various special or
short-term programs based on students’ needs.

✓ TOPIK Preparation Course: An intensive program designed to prepare

students for the TOPIK exam. It focuses on problem-solving practice
using actual past test questions.

passages.text:
(1) 외국인유학생 취업정보 제공

대한무역투자진흥공사(KOTRA) 해외전문인력유치센터(www.contactkorea.go.kr)와
한국유학종합시스템(www.studyinkorea.go.kr)에서 링크된 사이트를 통하여 유학생들은
구인구직 정보를 얻을 수 있다. 국립국제교육원은 매년 KOTRA와 함께 외국인유학생
채용박람회를 개최하고 있다.

76

(2) 외국인 과학기술자 고용추천서(사이언스카드)란?

외국인 고급과학기술인력에게 우리나라의 사증취득과 국내체류 관련(자격·활동·기간 등)
허가과정에서 편의를 제공함으로써 우수한 외국인 과학기술인력의 국내고용을 촉진하기
위해 과학기술정보통신부 장관이 발급하는 추천서

(3) 고용추천서(골드카드)란?

해외우수기술인재를 고용하고자 하는 기업에게 산업통상자원부 장관의 위임을 받아
KOTRA 사장 명의의 고용추천서 발급을 통해 특정활동비자(E-7) 발급을 지원하여 사증
및 체류 상의 우대를 부여하는 제도

passages.heading: Korea’s Education Structure
passages.text:
The Korean education system consists of a 16-year curriculum: 6 years of primary education, 6 years of secondary education (3 years of middle school, 3 years of high school).

Higher education institutions that international students can attend include 4-year universities, 2- to 3-year associate degree programs, and graduate schools offering master’s and doctoral
programs lasting 2 years or more.

passages.heading: Korea's Education System
passages.text:
Korea’s higher education system consists of bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degree programs offered by universities and vocational colleges,

as well as university-affiliated Korean language training programs.

passages.heading: From Studies to Employment
passages.text:
The number of international students who wish to work in Korea after graduation is increasing.

To support these students, dedicated job platforms for foreigners are available, and the Ministry of Education is expanding employment opportunities to help students find suitable jobs.

passages.heading: Job Preparation Process
passages.text:
International students can begin job seeking after converting their student visa to a job-seeking visa.

Internship opportunities in Korea are available for up to 6 months, and students can transition from short-term internships to long-term employment after graduation.

Long-term employment is also possible immediately after graduation. Be sure to check the Korean Language Proficiency Recognition Criteria before applying for jobs.

passages.heading: 2) Special Occupation (E-7)
passages.text:
A visa generally available for international students who get employed in Korea
after graduation. This is a type of employment visa issued to foreigners who wish
to work in professional or designated job positions under an employment contract
in Korea. Based on the level of specialization, the visa is categorized into Profes-
sional Workforce (E-7-1), Semi-Professional Workforce (E-7-2), General Skilled
Workforce (E-7-3), and Skilled Workforce (E-7-4). A set of occupations is allowed
depending on the job category (92 in all).

Eligible Applicants: 
Those who wish to engage in job positions (92 occupations) specifically
designated by the Minister of Justice according to the contract with Korean public
and private companies.

Allowed Period of Stay: 3 years, may be extended

Eligibility Requirements: 
Applicants must meet one of the following requirements to be eligible:
- Hold a master’s degree or higher in a field related to the occupation
- Hold a bachelor’s degree in a field related to the occupation and have at least one

year of work experience in the field
- Have at least five years' work experience in a field related to the occupation

※ Some requirements may be waived if the applicant meets the Special Conditions for Prefer-

ential Consideration.

Required Documents: 
- Valid passport, residence card (if applicable), integrated application form,

applicable fee, ID photo
- Original or copy of employment contract, proof of incorporation—i.e. business

registration certificate & certified copy of corporate registration, etc.
- Proof of tax payment history—employer’s tax receipt or company financial

passages.heading: Job Opportunities and Position Types
passages.text:
There are numerous opportunities for international students to find employment in various fields.

Depending on their major, nationality, and language skills, international students can find diverse jobs and roles. It is recommended to seek positions related to their major and practical
experiences.

- ### Language Teacher Responsible for teaching foreign languages such as Korean, English, Chinese, etc.
- ### Interpreter and Translator Handles multilingual translation tasks.
- ### Trade and Tourism Roles Provides tourism information and guidance services for foreign tourists.
- ### Automotive, Shipbuilding, Aviation, and Railway Engineering Specialist Researches, designs, and consults on engines used in automobiles, ships, airplanes, and railways, as well as supervises, controls, and advises on their manufacturing and operation.
- ### Medical Coordinator Provides comprehensive services for foreign patients, including guidance and support for medical visits,

appointment scheduling, interpretation, and customer management.
- ### IT Sector Roles Handles roles such as software development, system operation, and network management in the IT field.
- ### Design Field Handles various design tasks such as UI/UX, web design, advertising, graphic design, and fashion design.
- ### Marketing Tasks Responsible for tasks such as multilingual content creation, exploring overseas markets, customer support, and marketing promotions.
- ### Academic Research Field Handles positions such as research assistant, teaching assistant, or researcher at universities and companies.
- ### HR, Accounting, and Management Fields Handles HR, accounting, and management roles within companies.

Can I return to my home country during a leave of
absence from school?

For changes in academic status such as leave of
absence or graduation, your school is required to
report the change to the competent immigration
office.

Once the immigration office receives the report,
the student is regarded as not attending the
school and will be provided with departure guid-
ance. If the student has already left the country,
the Student visa will be terminated regardless
of any remaining period of stay. Therefore, the
student must obtain a new visa to reenter the
country.

I graduated in February. Can I leave the country for
a short period and return before the period of stay
expires, since it is valid until March?

The immigration office gets notified of the grad-
uation by the school and reviews the student’s
residence status. If the student has already left
the country, the Student visa will be considered
terminated regardless of any remaining period of
stay. Therefore, the visa will be terminated.

If you plan to pursue a higher degree or find em-
ployment in Korea after graduating from university,
we recommend extending your period of stay
or obtaining approval for a change of visa status
before leaving the country.

passages.heading: Recruitment Process
passages.text:
Work at a Korean company, the following process is generally followed.

- **1 Review Job Announcements** Job announcements from Korean companies can be found on company websites or recruitment platforms, where you can learn about job roles and responsibilities.
- **2 Application Submission** Applications and resumes must be submitted according to the job posting requirements. Your application and resume should include details about your experience, education, and certifications, as well as your reasons for applying. Importantly, as interviews will be based on the content of your documents, ensure your cover letter clearly demonstrates your capabilities and how they align with the job responsibilities.
- **3 Document Screening** The company evaluates applicants' academic background, work experience, certifications, and language skills based on the submitted documents.
- **4 Interview Process** During the interview, the applicant's personality, competencies, and technical skills are assessed. Depending on the company, the process may include a first-round technical interview, a second-round personality interview, or stages like a first-round technical and presentation interview followed by a second-round executive interview.
- **5 Final Selection** The final candidates for employment are selected.

The above process represents a typical recruitment procedure but may vary by company. In addition, international

students must follow extra steps, such as obtaining a work visa, so they should not only understand the domestic recruitment process but also check the employment qualifications and document
requirements.

passages.heading: 6. Practical job-search process
passages.text:
1. Search verified postings, your university career center, official campus boards, or reputable job websites (e.g., Albamon, Alba Heaven).
1. Ask the employer if they can provide an employment contract and business registration certificate and support a D-2/D-4 permit application.
1. Check job duties, working hours, wage, workplace address, start date, and pay method before signing.
1. Complete university verification, submit the immigration request, and keep proof of approval.
1. Keep copies of the contract, time records, payslips and permit; do not work outside approved conditions.

passages.heading: Job Opportunities and Position Types
passages.text:
There are numerous opportunities for international students to find employment in various fields.

Depending on their major, nationality, and language skills, international students can find diverse jobs and roles. It is recommended to seek positions related to their major and practical
experiences.

- ### Language Teacher Responsible for teaching foreign languages such as Korean, English, Chinese, etc.
- ### Interpreter and Translator Handles multilingual translation tasks.
- ### Trade and Tourism Roles Provides tourism information and guidance services for foreign tourists.
- ### Automotive, Shipbuilding, Aviation, and Railway Engineering Specialist Researches, designs, and consults on engines used in automobiles, ships, airplanes, and railways, as well as supervises, controls, and advises on their manufacturing and operation.
- ### Medical Coordinator Provides comprehensive services for foreign patients, including guidance and support for medical visits,

appointment scheduling, interpretation, and customer management.
- ### IT Sector Roles Handles roles such as software development, system operation, and network management in the IT field.
- ### Design Field Handles various design tasks such as UI/UX, web design, advertising, graphic design, and fashion design.
- ### Marketing Tasks Responsible for tasks such as multilingual content creation, exploring overseas markets, customer support, and marketing promotions.
- ### Academic Research Field Handles positions such as research assistant, teaching assistant, or researcher at universities and companies.
- ### HR, Accounting, and Management Fields Handles HR, accounting, and management roles within companies.

passages.heading: FAQ 5. I moved to a new dormitory. Do I need to notify immigration?
passages.text: An actual change of registered place of stay generally must be reported within 15 days, even if you stay within the same university area. Verify whether a room-only change altered the registered address.

passages.heading: 3) Visiting Healthcare Providers
passages.text:
Mandatory ID check

Pursuant to the National Health Insurance Act, individuals visiting a healthcare
provider must verify their identity by presenting a valid ID card before receiving
medical services. Medical services cannot be provided without presenting an ID
card. Acceptable forms of identification include those with a photo and a foreign
resident registration number, such as a residence card, passport,
or driver's license issued in Korea. A mobile health insurance
card can also be used in place of a physical ID card.

Mobile Health
Insurance Card App

Google Play
App Store

36

How to
Use the Mobile
Health Insurance Card

Install the app and verify your identification
through an authentication method.

Set a passcode or register your biometric
authentication information.

Tap "See the Health Insurance Card" or
"Identification QR for Eligibility for Health
Insurance" and present it at the reception
desk of the medical provider.

Visiting Hospitals by Symptom

Visit a hospital that offers the appropriate medical services indicated on its sign.

passages.heading: 1) National Health Insurance (NHI)
passages.text:
All international students staying in Korea for six months or longer are automatically
enrolled in the insurance as local subscribers* to NHI, receiving the same insurance
benefits as Korean nationals.
* Persons who register individually rather than as company employees

NHI Registration Process

Enter Korea
Register as a foreign
resident (must register
within 90 days of entry)

Automatic enrollment in
NHI (no separate application

required)

Pay a monthly health

insurance premium
The National Health Insurance Service

(NHIS) sends a notification letter
regarding registration and payment

※ Healthcare costs may be covered through a private health insurance plan until foreign resi-

dent registration is completed after entering Korea.

National Health Insurance Premiums Calculation

The NHI premium for international students is calculated un-
der the same standards applied to local Korean subscribers,
considering each student as a single household. However,
students holding a residency status eligible for abatement
[i.e., Student (D-2), General Trainee (D-4)] and whose
monthly income and assets are below the standards set by
NHI may receive a 50% discount on the monthly premium.

NHI Information for

Foreigners

※ Short-term visitors who stay in Korea for up to six months (e.g., exchange students, trainees)

are not eligible for automatic enrollment in NHI. However, some schools require international
students to register for a private health insurance plan or a group insurance plan, so please
check in advance.

※ Failure to pay the NHI premium will result in loss of coverage and higher medical expenses.

Please note that this may also affect visa extension eligibility.

passages.heading: 3) Visiting Healthcare Providers
passages.text:
Mandatory ID check

Pursuant to the National Health Insurance Act, individuals visiting a healthcare
provider must verify their identity by presenting a valid ID card before receiving
medical services. Medical services cannot be provided without presenting an ID
card. Acceptable forms of identification include those with a photo and a foreign
resident registration number, such as a residence card, passport,
or driver's license issued in Korea. A mobile health insurance
card can also be used in place of a physical ID card.

passages.heading: 5. Frequently asked questions (retrieval targets)
passages.text:
Q. Why did I receive an NHIS bill?

A. You may have been enrolled under mandatory foreign-resident health insurance rules; check the notice and visa-specific eligibility.

Q. Is every hospital visit free?

A. No. Benefits and patient co-payments differ by service.

Q. Can I be exempt if I have private insurance?

A. Only where an NHIS-recognized exclusion applies; contact NHIS with evidence.

passages.heading: Overview and recommended steps
passages.text:
- For life-threatening illness, injury, or loss of consciousness, call 119 immediately.
- For routine care, locate a clinic (의원) or hospital (병원) appropriate to symptoms, confirm opening hours and appointment requirements, and ask about availability of interpretation when necessary.
- Bring identification, your residence card or passport, and insurance information. Clinics and hospitals may verify NHIS eligibility through identity checks.
- NHIS gives official guidance on foreigner enrollment and exclusions, including circumstances involving qualifying alternative coverage. Verify your own coverage and payment status directly with NHIS.
- Ask the provider what portion of treatment and prescriptions is covered, what must be paid personally, and whether referrals are needed for certain hospital services.
- Keep prescriptions, visit receipts, and medical certificates if needed for university absence or insurer claims. For coverage or eligibility issues, contact NHIS foreign resident service channels.

passages.heading: 1. Plain-language answer
passages.text: TOPIK is the official Test of Proficiency in Korean. TOPIK I assesses beginner levels (1-2) and TOPIK II assesses intermediate/advanced levels (3-6). Registration windows, exam format, fees and locations vary by test round and country.

passages.heading: 5. Frequently asked questions (retrieval targets)
passages.text:
Q. Which test should I take for level 4?

A. TOPIK II is the test for levels 3-6.

Q. Can I sign up at any time?

A. No. Registration is only open during announced windows and capacity can fill.

Q. Does passing TOPIK automatically grant part-time employment permission?

A. No. Language ability is only one possible eligibility factor; immigration permission may still be required.

passages.heading: 2. Rules and eligibility
passages.text:
- TOPIK I covers levels 1-2; TOPIK II covers levels 3-6.
- Paper-based and Internet-based test formats may have distinct schedules and registration procedures.
- Test registration is separate from university scholarship, graduation, and immigration rules; each institution sets applicable accepted level.
- Registration schedules and available seats are time-sensitive; always cite the live official TOPIK announcement.

passages.heading: Overview and recommended steps
passages.text:
- Check the expiry date on your residence status in advance. A D-2 student who needs more time to study must apply for extension of stay before their authorized stay expires.
- Confirm continued enrollment and the university’s international office instructions. The immigration office can require additional evidence based on study progress and personal circumstances.
- Use the official Stay Extension guidance, then check HiKorea for online application eligibility or reservation. Do not assume an online option exists for every case.
- Prepare the application, passport, residence card, evidence of enrollment or ongoing study, evidence of residence, and any additional items specified for your D-2 subtype. Proof of finances, tuition payment, or academic progress may be required in individual cases.
- Submit the application through the permitted route before expiry, pay the assessed fee, and retain application/receipt information. Follow requests for supplemental evidence.
- Do not treat application submission as automatic approval; verify your status and any travel restrictions while an extension is pending.

passages.heading: Can I travel with a pending extension?
passages.text: Consult immigration before booking travel.

passages.heading: Overseas travel or visa extension
passages.text: Address reporting and extension of stay are distinct immigration procedures. Completing one does not automatically mean every other required report has been completed. Confirm the correct registered address when extending a visa.

passages.heading: Overview and recommended steps
passages.text:
- Before departure, check your passport validity, residence-card validity, current authorized stay, and any pending visa/status application.
- The Ministry of Justice announced a re-entry permit exemption for many registered foreigners returning within one year; the exemption is limited by the remaining period of authorized stay and immigration exceptions. Confirm that the policy still applies to your status and travel dates.
- Do not assume an expired residence card or an extension application guarantees admission back into Korea.
- Ask immigration (1345) before international travel if your status is changing, renewal is pending, your residence card is lost, or you will be outside Korea for an extended period.
- Check the destination country’s entry/visa requirements, your airline’s document requirements, and any transit visa obligations.
- On return, carry passport, residence card where applicable, and evidence of student status if useful. Border officials make the final entry determination.
