89

I left the country after submitting a civil petition
to the immigration office. Can the office review
the matter while I’m overseas or handle it after I
reenter the country?

If an applicant is confirmed to have left the country
during the review process, the review will be
suspended or may be terminated at the discretion
of the immigration officer.

This is because the inquiry cannot remain unre-
solved for an extended period when it is uncertain
whether the applicant will return to the country,
and it is difficult to obtain additional information
when further confirmation is needed during the
review. Therefore, please make your inquiry with
your departure schedule in mind. In unavoidable
circumstances, you should submit the inquiry
again after reentering the country.

I plan to return to my home country after gradua-
tion, and this will terminate my visa. Is there a way
to get employed after I return to Korea?

We recommend obtaining approval for a visa
change before leaving the country if you plan to
look for a job after graduation or if your employ-
ment has already been confirmed.

If you do not have enough time, you may apply for
a Job Seeker (D-10) visa after leaving the country.
If this is your first Job Seeker (D-10) visa after
graduation and it is within one year of your grad-
uation date, you will be exempted from the point-
based system.

passages.heading: 5) Change in Visa Status
passages.text:
This refers to a situation wherein a foreign national residing in Korea intends to dis-
continue the activity permitted under his/her current visa and begin a new activity
that falls under a different visa category. <e.g., Student (D-2) → Job seeking (D-10)>

In principle, foreigners who intend to change their visa status must leave the coun-
try, obtain the new visa, and reenter Korea. Under limited circumstances, however,
a change of visa status may be allowed within Korea following a stringent review
process, provided the applicant meets the eligibility requirements for the new visa.

※ Permission for a change in visa status must be obtained from the competent Immigration

Office before engaging in any activity that falls under a different visa category

Can I return to my home country during a leave of
absence from school?

For changes in academic status such as leave of
absence or graduation, your school is required to
report the change to the competent immigration
office.

Once the immigration office receives the report,
the student is regarded as not attending the
school and will be provided with departure guid-
ance. If the student has already left the country,
the Student visa will be terminated regardless
of any remaining period of stay. Therefore, the
student must obtain a new visa to reenter the
country.

I graduated in February. Can I leave the country for
a short period and return before the period of stay
expires, since it is valid until March?

The immigration office gets notified of the grad-
uation by the school and reviews the student’s
residence status. If the student has already left
the country, the Student visa will be considered
terminated regardless of any remaining period of
stay. Therefore, the visa will be terminated.

If you plan to pursue a higher degree or find em-
ployment in Korea after graduating from university,
we recommend extending your period of stay
or obtaining approval for a change of visa status
before leaving the country.

passages.heading: Visa Screening and Issuance Results
passages.text:
Upon receiving a visa application, the head of a diplomatic mission abroad or the Minister of Justice can issue the visa.

However, a review will be conducted prior to issuance to ensure that the applicant meets the eligibility criteria.

- Possession of a valid passport.
- Not being subject to entry prohibition or denial under Article 11 of the Immigration Act.
- Eligibility for the visa type under the Immigration Act Enforcement Decree.
- Providing a valid purpose of entry consistent with the visa type.
- Demonstrating intent to return to the home country within the permitted duration of stay.
- Meeting additional criteria specified by the Minister of Justice for the specific visa type.

passages.text:
89

I left the country after submitting a civil petition
to the immigration office. Can the office review
the matter while I’m overseas or handle it after I
reenter the country?

If an applicant is confirmed to have left the country
during the review process, the review will be
suspended or may be terminated at the discretion
of the immigration officer.

This is because the inquiry cannot remain unre-
solved for an extended period when it is uncertain
whether the applicant will return to the country,
and it is difficult to obtain additional information
when further confirmation is needed during the
review. Therefore, please make your inquiry with
your departure schedule in mind. In unavoidable
circumstances, you should submit the inquiry
again after reentering the country.

I plan to return to my home country after gradua-
tion, and this will terminate my visa. Is there a way
to get employed after I return to Korea?

We recommend obtaining approval for a visa
change before leaving the country if you plan to
look for a job after graduation or if your employ-
ment has already been confirmed.

If you do not have enough time, you may apply for
a Job Seeker (D-10) visa after leaving the country.
If this is your first Job Seeker (D-10) visa after
graduation and it is within one year of your grad-
uation date, you will be exempted from the point-
based system.

90

I have stayed in Korea for up to six years—which
is the maximum permitted period of stay—while
completing my bachelor’s degree program at a
university. However, I still need to have my thesis
reviewed. Can I extend my period of stay?

passages.heading: 4. Extending period of stay (체류기간 연장)
passages.text:
A residence card is evidence of registered status. Its physical replacement is NOT the mechanism for permission to remain longer. A D-2 or D-4 student who needs to stay beyond the authorized expiry date must request extension of period of stay before expiry, with the evidence appropriate to the student and institution.

1. Check the authorized stay expiry date and current visa subtype; do not rely only on the plastic card’s appearance.
1. Ask the university international office whether it offers student-group extension or issues required enrollment, attendance and financial documents.
1. Check HiKorea for current eligibility for e-application or make a visit reservation.
1. Prepare passport, residence card, application form, fee, proof of enrollment and residence, and additional immigration-requested records.
1. Submit the application before the current permitted stay ends and follow any instructions for biometric/card updates or additional evidence.
Risk situations: taking leave of absence, withdrawing, graduating, changing universities, or ending a language program can affect the basis for student stay. Do not assume the printed expiry date guarantees permission after a change in academic status. Seek university and immigration advice promptly.

passages.heading: International Students
passages.text:
International students have a maximum allowable
period of stay for each degree program, so it is
not possible to extend beyond that limit. If you
have taken a leave of absence from school for two
semesters (one year) or more and have left and
reentered the country, the period spent abroad
may be excluded from the calculation of your total
period of stay.

Please refer to the table below for the maximum
period of stay when planning your academic
schedule.

Category
Maximum Stay Period

Associate Degree
Up to 3 years
(up to 4 years for 4-year programs)

Bachelor’s Degree
Up to 6 years
(up to 7 years for 5-year programs)

Master’s Degree
Up to 5 years
(up to 6 years for 3-year programs)

Doctoral Degree
Up to 8 years
(up to 7 years for 2-year programs)

I’d like to transfer to another school. I’ve already
been admitted to a new school. Can I apply for a
school transfer?

In principle, you are not allowed to transfer
between schools in Korea. You must leave the
country, obtain a new visa, and then return.

However, you may apply for a school transfer
if the reason for changing schools is deemed
unavoidable. Note that the total period of stay
must not exceed each duration of studies at the
current school and the new school. If you are
dismissed from your current school and subject to
departure, you will not be permitted to transfer.

passages.heading: 1) Job Seeker (D-10)
passages.text:
The visa obtained by foreigners when searching for a job, preparing for an
internship, or starting a new business. It is categorized into General Job-Seeking
(D-10-1), Preparing Tech Start-Up (D-10-2), and Internship in Advanced Technology
(D-10-3). The following section describes the General Job-Seeking (D-10-1) visa.

General Job-Seeking (D-10-1)

The relevant visa allows applicants to seek fields of employment or complete
internships corresponding to eligibility for the Professor (E-1) to Special Occupa-
tion (E-7) visa upon graduation from a Korean university. After securing full-time
employment, the E-series visa generally requires conversion to an E-7 visa.

Allowed Period of Stay:
1 year. Extensions are possible for up to 3 years.
※However, please note that the length of stay may vary depending on individual eligibility.

Application Period:
It is required to apply for a change in the D-10-1 visa status as soon as possible
after graduation.

Eligible Applicants:
(1) Applicants Subject to the Point-based Review System

Applicants must hold at least a bachelor's degree—including a Korean university
associate's degree—as a legal resident in Korea, and have a total score of 60 or
more, with at least 20 points in the baseline items out of a total of 190 points on
the Job Search Score Sheet*
*The visa status is issued based on a points-based review system and must meet the score
requirements.
(2) Applicants Exempted from the Point-based Review System

passages.heading: 2. Rules and eligibility
passages.text:
- Apply for change of stay status before engaging in activity that requires the new status.
- Changing from D-4 language training to D-2 study or D-2 graduation to D-10/E-series employment is not automatic.
- Application feasibility and supporting evidence depend on current visa subtype, destination visa subtype, academic achievements and immigration history.
- A university acceptance or employer offer is not the same as status-change approval.

I left the country after submitting a civil petition
to the immigration office. Can the office review
the matter while I’m overseas or handle it after I
reenter the country?

If an applicant is confirmed to have left the country
during the review process, the review will be
suspended or may be terminated at the discretion
of the immigration officer.

This is because the inquiry cannot remain unre-
solved for an extended period when it is uncertain
whether the applicant will return to the country,
and it is difficult to obtain additional information
when further confirmation is needed during the
review. Therefore, please make your inquiry with
your departure schedule in mind. In unavoidable
circumstances, you should submit the inquiry
again after reentering the country.

I plan to return to my home country after gradua-

to get employed after I return to Korea?

We recommend obtaining approval for a visa
change before leaving the country if you plan to
look for a job after graduation or if your employ-
ment has already been confirmed.

If you do not have enough time, you may apply for
a Job Seeker (D-10) visa after leaving the country.
If this is your first Job Seeker (D-10) visa after
graduation and it is within one year of your grad-
uation date, you will be exempted from the point-
based system.

passages.heading: 5. Frequently asked questions (retrieval targets)
passages.text:
Q. Can I begin my university degree with a D-4 visa?

A. Check whether a D-2 status change is required and secure approval before commencing activities requiring D-2.

Q. Does a job offer convert my visa automatically?

A. No. Immigration approval is required for a change of status when applicable.

Q. Can everyone apply for D-10?

A. No. Eligibility and exclusions depend on individual history and criteria.

passages.heading: 2. Rules and eligibility
passages.text:
- Apply for change of stay status before engaging in activity that requires the new status.
- Changing from D-4 language training to D-2 study or D-2 graduation to D-10/E-series employment is not automatic.
- Application feasibility and supporting evidence depend on current visa subtype, destination visa subtype, academic achievements and immigration history.
- A university acceptance or employer offer is not the same as status-change approval.

passages.heading: Overview and recommended steps
passages.text:
- Check the expiry date on your residence status in advance. A D-2 student who needs more time to study must apply for extension of stay before their authorized stay expires.
- Confirm continued enrollment and the university’s international office instructions. The immigration office can require additional evidence based on study progress and personal circumstances.
- Use the official Stay Extension guidance, then check HiKorea for online application eligibility or reservation. Do not assume an online option exists for every case.
- Prepare the application, passport, residence card, evidence of enrollment or ongoing study, evidence of residence, and any additional items specified for your D-2 subtype. Proof of finances, tuition payment, or academic progress may be required in individual cases.
- Submit the application through the permitted route before expiry, pay the assessed fee, and retain application/receipt information. Follow requests for supplemental evidence.
- Do not treat application submission as automatic approval; verify your status and any travel restrictions while an extension is pending.

passages.heading: 5. Frequently asked questions (retrieval targets)
passages.text:
Q. Can I begin my university degree with a D-4 visa?

A. Check whether a D-2 status change is required and secure approval before commencing activities requiring D-2.

Q. Does a job offer convert my visa automatically?

A. No. Immigration approval is required for a change of status when applicable.

Q. Can everyone apply for D-10?

A. No. Eligibility and exclusions depend on individual history and criteria.

Internship Requirements

Whether Eligible for Part-time Positions

In principle, international students are not allowed to engage in part-time
employment. However, they may work part-time within limited hours and
approved job categories after obtaining permission for part-time employment,
provided they meet certain requirements.

passages.heading: 5. Types of work
passages.text:
- Ordinary student-type part-time work may include restaurant assistance, general office assistance, tourism-related support, and retail/duty-free sales assistance, subject to individual approval. [S2]
- Special professional activities and private tutoring may follow other rules; private tutoring is especially restricted. [S1]
- Do NOT assume delivery work, platform/gig work, construction work, freelance work, or work at a second workplace is allowed. Ask the immigration office before committing.
- Changing employer, worksite, role, or schedule can affect authorization. Check reporting or new-permit requirements before changing anything.

passages.heading: Part-Time Work for International Students (Part-Time Jobs)
passages.text:

최근 법무부 및 출입국·외국인청에서 외국인 유학생 대상 불법취업(무단 아르바이트) 집중 단속 및 조사를 실시하고 있습니다.

특히 SNS, 오픈채팅 및 외국인 대상 구인 어플리케이션 등을 통한 불법 근로 연계 사례가 다수 확인되고 있으며, 실제 출입국사무소 조사 및 출석 요구 사례도 발생하고 있습니다.

최근에는 외국인 구인 플랫폼인 Face One 등을 통해 단기·일용성 아르바이트를 연결받아 적발되는 사례가 증가하고 있으니 각별히 주의하시기 바랍니다.

1. 불법취업 해당 사례

- 시간제취업 허가 없이 근로 진행
- 허가받은 근무시간 초과 근로

- 허가받지 않은 업종·사업장 근무

- Face One 등 외국인 대상 구인 어플을 통한 단기 아르바이트 참여

- 현금 지급 형태의 무신고 근로

- 행사 보조, 통역, 판매, 홍보, 물류 업무 등 일용성 단기 근로

- SNS·오픈채팅을 통한 아르바이트 참여

※ “하루만”, “단기”, “현금 지급”, “외국인 가능” 형태의 모집도 모두 단속 대상이 될 수 있습니다.

2. 적발 시 불이익

- 범칙금 부과

- 출입국사무소 출석 및 조사

- 시간제취업 허가 제한

- 체류기간 연장 제한

- 비자 변경 및 체류 심사 불이익

- 강제퇴거(추방) 조치

※ 위반 기간 및 횟수에 따라 범칙금이 크게 증가할 수 있으며, 중대한 위반으로 판단될 경우 강제퇴거 대상이 될 수 있습니다.

<불법취업 기간별 주요 범칙금 사례>

- 1개월 이상 : 약 300만원 수준 범칙금 부과 가능

- 6개월 이상 : 약 700만원 수준 범칙금 부과 가능

- 장기·반복 위반 : 강제퇴거 대상 포함 가능

3. 유의사항

최근 “단기 알바”, “하루 일당”, “통역 가능자 모집”, “외국인 가능” 등의 형태로 불법 근로 모집 사례가 증가하고 있습니다.

“다른 학생들도 하고 있다”, “잠깐만 도와주는 것이다”, “현금 지급이라 문제없다” 등의 안내를 받더라도, 적발 시 모든 책임은 본인에게 있습니다.

passages.text:
- Ordinary student-type part-time work may include restaurant assistance, general office assistance, tourism-related support, and retail/duty-free sales assistance, subject to individual approval. [S2]

2. 적발 시 불이익

- 범칙금 부과

- 출입국사무소 출석 및 조사

- 시간제취업 허가 제한

- 체류기간 연장 제한

- 비자 변경 및 체류 심사 불이익

- 강제퇴거(추방) 조치

※ 위반 기간 및 횟수에 따라 범칙금이 크게 증가할 수 있으며, 중대한 위반으로 판단될 경우 강제퇴거 대상이 될 수 있습니다.

<불법취업 기간별 주요 범칙금 사례>

- 1개월 이상 : 약 300만원 수준 범칙금 부과 가능

- 6개월 이상 : 약 700만원 수준 범칙금 부과 가능

- 장기·반복 위반 : 강제퇴거 대상 포함 가능

3. 유의사항

최근 “단기 알바”, “하루 일당”, “통역 가능자 모집”, “외국인 가능” 등의 형태로 불법 근로 모집 사례가 증가하고 있습니다.

“다른 학생들도 하고 있다”, “잠깐만 도와주는 것이다”, “현금 지급이라 문제없다” 등의 안내를 받더라도, 적발 시 모든 책임은 본인에게 있습니다.

최근 법무부 및 출입국·외국인청에서 외국인 유학생 대상 불법취업(무단 아르바이트) 집중 단속 및 조사를 실시하고 있습니다.

특히 SNS, 오픈채팅 및 외국인 대상 구인 어플리케이션 등을 통한 불법 근로 연계 사례가 다수 확인되고 있으며, 실제 출입국사무소 조사 및 출석 요구 사례도 발생하고 있습니다.

최근에는 외국인 구인 플랫폼인 Face One 등을 통해 단기·일용성 아르바이트를 연결받아 적발되는 사례가 증가하고 있으니 각별히 주의하시기 바랍니다.

1. 불법취업 해당 사례

- 시간제취업 허가 없이 근로 진행
- 허가받은 근무시간 초과 근로

- 허가받지 않은 업종·사업장 근무

- Face One 등 외국인 대상 구인 어플을 통한 단기 아르바이트 참여

- 현금 지급 형태의 무신고 근로

- 행사 보조, 통역, 판매, 홍보, 물류 업무 등 일용성 단기 근로

- SNS·오픈채팅을 통한 아르바이트 참여

passages.heading: 5. Types of work
passages.text:
- Ordinary student-type part-time work may include restaurant assistance, general office assistance, tourism-related support, and retail/duty-free sales assistance, subject to individual approval. [S2]
- Special professional activities and private tutoring may follow other rules; private tutoring is especially restricted. [S1]
- Do NOT assume delivery work, platform/gig work, construction work, freelance work, or work at a second workplace is allowed. Ask the immigration office before committing.

passages.heading: 6. Practical job-search process
passages.text:
1. Search verified postings, your university career center, official campus boards, or reputable job websites (e.g., Albamon, Alba Heaven).
1. Ask the employer if they can provide an employment contract and business registration certificate and support a D-2/D-4 permit application.
1. Check job duties, working hours, wage, workplace address, start date, and pay method before signing.
1. Complete university verification, submit the immigration request, and keep proof of approval.
1. Keep copies of the contract, time records, payslips and permit; do not work outside approved conditions.

start working right away. Can I begin work?

Student visa holders are not allowed to work
in Korea without permission. If you receive
confirmation from your university and approval

commonly performed by college students.

apply for permission for part-time employment

passages.heading: 1. Core answer: How do I legally start a part-time job?
passages.text:
1. Find an employer willing to hire an eligible international student; confirm the job category is allowed.
1. Sign a standard employment contract (근로계약서) specifying hourly wage, duties, location, hours and dates.
1. Complete the Part-Time Employment Confirmation Form (외국인 유학생 시간제취업 확인서) with confirmation/signature from the university international-student advisor.
1. Submit the application and supporting documents through HiKorea (when the relevant online service is available) or at the immigration office.
1. Receive approval (online printable permission or an approval sticker, as applicable) BEFORE starting work. Work only within the permitted conditions.
Official source: Study in Korea, “Part-Time Work for International Students,” section Approval Process [S1].

passages.heading: Penalties for Unauthorized Employment
passages.text:
If you work without obtaining part-time employment permission or violate the conditions of your permitted employment, you will be penalized under the law.

※ For illegal employment in the construction sector, deportation orders are issued without exception, regardless of the number of violations. However, entry restrictions may be deferred.

passages.heading: International Students
passages.text:
91

I am currently a language trainee but plan to study
at a university. I’d like to apply for an interim visa
and I want to know the requirements.

You can apply for a visa called an interim visa if the
period between the end of your current stay and
the start of the new semester is three months or
less. To be eligible, you must meet all three of the
following requirements:

① A student in a language training program

who meets the visa extension requirements,
including attendance rate;

② A student who has successfully completed

the language training program and who has
been admitted to a degree program equivalent
to an associate degree or higher at the same
university. If the student is admitted to a
different university, the new school must be a
general university or higher;

③ A student with TOPIK score of Level 3 or higher,

or a student who has stayed in Korea for 18
months or longer with a Language Student visa
and with proven Korean language proficiency.

I have applied for foreign resident registration, but I
moved to my friend’s home and my home address
has changed. What should I do?

If your home address has changed, you must
report the change of residence within 15 days. If
you did not sign the residence contract yourself
and you are staying at a provided residence
instead, you must submit (1) the lease agreement,
(2) a confirmation letter stating that the residence
is being provided, and (3) a copy of the residence
provider’s (friend’s) ID card.

passages.heading: FAQ 5. I moved to a new dormitory. Do I need to notify immigration?
passages.text: An actual change of registered place of stay generally must be reported within 15 days, even if you stay within the same university area. Verify whether a room-only change altered the registered address.

passages.heading: 1. Important rules at a glance
passages.text:
| Procedure | Key information |
| First foreigner registration | Generally within 90 days after entering Korea when intending to stay over 90 days. |
| Initial application | Use HiKorea visit reservation and apply at the immigration office with jurisdiction over residence; some universities coordinate group submissions. |
| Physical card fee | KRW 35,000 for issuance/reissuance since 1 January 2025; other immigration service fees can apply separately. |
| Lost card | Report loss on HiKorea to reduce misuse risk, then separately apply for reissuance promptly. |
| Stay renewal | Extend permitted period of stay BEFORE expiration; replacing the plastic card alone does not extend status. |
| Address change | Registered foreigners generally report their new residence within 15 days after moving. |
| Passport information | Report applicable changes; the passport-reporting deadline has special rules, so check the current HiKorea notice or 1345. |

Important distinction: “ARC renewal” is colloquial. Government immigration procedures distinguish extension of period of stay (체류기간 연장), reissuance of a residence card (등록증 재발급), and reporting changes to registration details (등록사항 변경신고).

passages.heading: 5. Changes to registered information (등록사항 변경신고)
passages.text:
Students must distinguish changes in identity/passport records from changes in their place of stay. The required channel, evidence and reporting deadline differ.

| Change | Deadline / distinction | Action |
| Moved to a different residence (체류지 변경신고) | Generally within 15 days after moving for registered foreign residents. | Report via eligible HiKorea e-service, local government office or immigration office; provide new proof of residence. |
| New passport / passport number (여권정보 변경신고) | Special passport-reporting rules apply; do not automatically use the address deadline. | Older official Visa Navigator guidance mentions 45 days after passport issuance and a receipt-date exception; verify current rule and accepted proof. |
| Name, nationality, sex, date of birth or other registration particulars (등록사항 변경신고) | A reporting obligation can apply, often within a short statutory period. | Check exact trigger, deadline and required documentary evidence with immigration before submitting. |
| Change of visa status (체류자격 변경허가) | Permission generally needed before activities of the new status. | This is a status application, not merely a card-details update. |

For address-change details, link this article to the separate RAG article “Change of Address in South Korea”.

passages.text:
| Procedure | Key information |
| First foreigner registration | Generally within 90 days after entering Korea when intending to stay over 90 days. |
| Initial application | Use HiKorea visit reservation and apply at the immigration office with jurisdiction over residence; some universities coordinate group submissions. |
| Physical card fee | KRW 35,000 for issuance/reissuance since 1 January 2025; other immigration service fees can apply separately. |
| Lost card | Report loss on HiKorea to reduce misuse risk, then separately apply for reissuance promptly. |
| Stay renewal | Extend permitted period of stay BEFORE expiration; replacing the plastic card alone does not extend status. |
| Address change | Registered foreigners generally report their new residence within 15 days after moving. |
| Passport information | Report applicable changes; the passport-reporting deadline has special rules, so check the current HiKorea notice or 1345. |

Important distinction: “ARC renewal” is colloquial. Government immigration procedures distinguish extension of period of stay (체류기간 연장), reissuance of a residence card (등록증 재발급), and reporting changes to registration details (등록사항 변경신고).

“다른 학생들도 하고 있다”, “잠깐만 도와주는 것이다”, “현금 지급이라 문제없다” 등의 안내를 받더라도, 적발 시 모든 책임은 본인에게 있습니다.

passages.heading: 3) Reporting Changes to Foreigner Registration Information
passages.text:
International students must report any changes in their registration information to
the competent Immigration Office within 15 days of the change, if such changes
fall under the categories listed below.

Reasons for Updating Foreigner Registration Information
• Change of name, gender, date of birth, or nationality

• Change of passport number, issuance date, expiration date

• Change of school information (including the name)

Report Deadline
Within 15 days of the change

Where to Report
Competent Immigration Office or Online (HiKorea)

Required Documents
• Application form, passport, residence card

passages.heading: 5. Changes to registered information (등록사항 변경신고)
passages.text:
Students must distinguish changes in identity/passport records from changes in their place of stay. The required channel, evidence and reporting deadline differ.

| Change | Deadline / distinction | Action |
| Moved to a different residence (체류지 변경신고) | Generally within 15 days after moving for registered foreign residents. | Report via eligible HiKorea e-service, local government office or immigration office; provide new proof of residence. |
| New passport / passport number (여권정보 변경신고) | Special passport-reporting rules apply; do not automatically use the address deadline. | Older official Visa Navigator guidance mentions 45 days after passport issuance and a receipt-date exception; verify current rule and accepted proof. |
| Name, nationality, sex, date of birth or other registration particulars (등록사항 변경신고) | A reporting obligation can apply, often within a short statutory period. | Check exact trigger, deadline and required documentary evidence with immigration before submitting. |
| Change of visa status (체류자격 변경허가) | Permission generally needed before activities of the new status. | This is a status application, not merely a card-details update. |

For address-change details, link this article to the separate RAG article “Change of Address in South Korea”.

passages.heading: Q: Do I need to report if I move to another city?
passages.text: A: Yes. A registered foreign resident must report a changed place of stay, using the competent office for the new address. [S1]

passages.heading: Immediate action and replacement steps
passages.text:
1. If lost, use HiKorea → Information Inquiry (정보조회) → Report Lost Residence Card (등록증·거소증 분실(철회) 신고) to reduce misuse risk.
1. Check whether theft requires a police report for personal or insurance reasons; request assistance from the university or 1345 when needed.
1. Arrange a replacement-card (재발급) application through the appropriate immigration channel; a loss report by itself is not a new card.
1. Bring passport, integrated application form, photograph if requested, evidence of loss/damage if applicable, old card when damaged, and the current reissuance fee.
1. Keep submission evidence and confirm any travel, banking, or identity-verification needs with the relevant institution while the card is absent.
Timing caution: older official guidance specifies prompt reissuance after loss, including a 14-day requirement. Because the latest applicable rule and filing arrangements may change, verify the current deadline at HiKorea or immigration 1345 immediately rather than waiting.

If the card is found after reporting it lost, ask immigration how to withdraw the loss report and whether the original card remains usable. Do not assume it is automatically valid.

passages.heading: 5) Change in Visa Status
passages.text:
This refers to a situation wherein a foreign national residing in Korea intends to dis-
continue the activity permitted under his/her current visa and begin a new activity
that falls under a different visa category. <e.g., Student (D-2) → Job seeking (D-10)>

In principle, foreigners who intend to change their visa status must leave the coun-
try, obtain the new visa, and reenter Korea. Under limited circumstances, however,
a change of visa status may be allowed within Korea following a stringent review
process, provided the applicant meets the eligibility requirements for the new visa.

※ Permission for a change in visa status must be obtained from the competent Immigration

passages.heading: 5. Changes to registered information (등록사항 변경신고)
passages.text:
Students must distinguish changes in identity/passport records from changes in their place of stay. The required channel, evidence and reporting deadline differ.

| Change | Deadline / distinction | Action |
| Moved to a different residence (체류지 변경신고) | Generally within 15 days after moving for registered foreign residents. | Report via eligible HiKorea e-service, local government office or immigration office; provide new proof of residence. |
| New passport / passport number (여권정보 변경신고) | Special passport-reporting rules apply; do not automatically use the address deadline. | Older official Visa Navigator guidance mentions 45 days after passport issuance and a receipt-date exception; verify current rule and accepted proof. |
| Name, nationality, sex, date of birth or other registration particulars (등록사항 변경신고) | A reporting obligation can apply, often within a short statutory period. | Check exact trigger, deadline and required documentary evidence with immigration before submitting. |
| Change of visa status (체류자격 변경허가) | Permission generally needed before activities of the new status. | This is a status application, not merely a card-details update. |

passages.heading: FAQ 5. I moved to a new dormitory. Do I need to notify immigration?
passages.text: An actual change of registered place of stay generally must be reported within 15 days, even if you stay within the same university area. Verify whether a room-only change altered the registered address.

passages.heading: 2. Who must report and when
passages.text:
- Generally: registered foreign residents who change their registered place of stay, including D-2 degree students and D-4 language trainees. [S1]
- Deadline: within 15 days from the move-in date. Submit as early as possible rather than on the last day. [S1]
- If you have not yet completed first-time foreigner registration, the relevant procedure may be initial registration rather than change-of-address reporting. Confirm with immigration or the university. [S1]
- If you move to a different city or immigration district, report using the new location and the responsible office. [S1, S2]

passages.heading: FAQ 6. I received a new passport. Do I need to update immigration?
passages.text: Yes, applicable passport-detail changes must be reported. Check the current reporting deadline and proof rules on HiKorea or with 1345.

passages.heading: 3) Reporting Changes to Foreigner Registration Information
passages.text:
International students must report any changes in their registration information to
the competent Immigration Office within 15 days of the change, if such changes
fall under the categories listed below.

Reasons for Updating Foreigner Registration Information
• Change of name, gender, date of birth, or nationality

• Change of passport number, issuance date, expiration date

• Change of school information (including the name)

Report Deadline
Within 15 days of the change

Where to Report
Competent Immigration Office or Online (HiKorea)

Required Documents
• Application form, passport, residence card

• (Change of personal information including name) Document
verifying the change (applicable person)

• (Change of school) Certificate of enrollment and certificate of
withdrawal from the previous school (applicable person), and
document demonstrating the necessity of the school change
or explaining unavoidable circumstances (applicable person)

• (Change of school name) Document confirming the change of
school name, including the school's unique identification
number certificate

passages.heading: 8. Chatbot answer policy and escalation
passages.text:
- Answer the deadline first: report within 15 days of the actual move-in date. Cite official national sources. [S1]
- If documents are unclear, ask for the accommodation type (dormitory, lease, living with another person) rather than asking for a full address or ID number in chat.
- Do not collect or reproduce passport numbers, ARC numbers, copies of IDs, rental contracts or students’ precise home addresses in chatbot conversations.
- Escalate cases involving missed deadlines, conflicting residence evidence, pending first registration, disputed occupancy or system errors to immigration (1345) first. University supporter referral may help with interpretation and steps, but must not replace an official legal decision.
- For uncertain online navigation, link to the HiKorea homepage rather than inventing a direct form path.

passages.heading: Q: Does my school report my address automatically?
passages.text: A: Do not assume the school submits the immigration report. Verify that the immigration reporting requirement is satisfied and separately update your university record if required.

passages.heading: Dormitory to dormitory or dormitory to apartment
passages.text: If the registered residential address changes, report it even if you are staying at the same university. Check with your dormitory administration for a residence certificate. The university also may require a separate profile-address update.

passages.heading: Q: I moved from my university dorm to an apartment. What should I do?
passages.text: A: Report the new address within 15 days of moving. Prepare your residence card, passport, lease and any requested form. Apply via an eligible online service or at the local community center / immigration office. [S1, S2]

passages.heading: FAQ 5. I moved to a new dormitory. Do I need to notify immigration?
passages.text: An actual change of registered place of stay generally must be reported within 15 days, even if you stay within the same university area. Verify whether a room-only change altered the registered address.

passages.heading: 5. Changes to registered information (등록사항 변경신고)
passages.text:
Students must distinguish changes in identity/passport records from changes in their place of stay. The required channel, evidence and reporting deadline differ.

| Change | Deadline / distinction | Action |
| Moved to a different residence (체류지 변경신고) | Generally within 15 days after moving for registered foreign residents. | Report via eligible HiKorea e-service, local government office or immigration office; provide new proof of residence. |
| New passport / passport number (여권정보 변경신고) | Special passport-reporting rules apply; do not automatically use the address deadline. | Older official Visa Navigator guidance mentions 45 days after passport issuance and a receipt-date exception; verify current rule and accepted proof. |
| Name, nationality, sex, date of birth or other registration particulars (등록사항 변경신고) | A reporting obligation can apply, often within a short statutory period. | Check exact trigger, deadline and required documentary evidence with immigration before submitting. |
| Change of visa status (체류자격 변경허가) | Permission generally needed before activities of the new status. | This is a status application, not merely a card-details update. |

For address-change details, link this article to the separate RAG article “Change of Address in South Korea”.

passages.heading: 4. Step-by-step: Online report
passages.text:
1. Prepare your residence card (ARC), passport details, the exact new address and proof of occupancy.
1. Open https://www.hikorea.go.kr/ and sign in using an available verification method.
1. Find the electronic civil service for reporting a change of place of stay (체류지 변경신고); menus can change over time.
1. Complete the requested move-in date and new address, upload supporting documents and submit.
1. Check the application result, save confirmation and verify that your registered address was updated. If the online service is unavailable or rejects the submission, use an eligible in-person reporting channel before the deadline.

passages.heading: Dormitory to dormitory or dormitory to apartment
passages.text: If the registered residential address changes, report it even if you are staying at the same university. Check with your dormitory administration for a residence certificate. The university also may require a separate profile-address update.

passages.heading: 1. Key answer
passages.text:
Registered foreigners, including most D-2 and D-4 international students with residence registration, must report a change of their place of stay within 15 days of moving to the new address. This requirement applies even when moving between dormitory rooms or from a dormitory to off-campus housing if the registered residential address changes. Reporting late may result in an administrative fine, which can be up to KRW 1,000,000. [S1]

Use the actual address where you live. The immigration address-change report is separate from changing a mailing address at a bank, school, telephone provider or delivery app.

passages.heading: Q: I moved from my university dorm to an apartment. What should I do?
passages.text: A: Report the new address within 15 days of moving. Prepare your residence card, passport, lease and any requested form. Apply via an eligible online service or at the local community center / immigration office. [S1, S2]

passages.heading: FAQ 5. I moved to a new dormitory. Do I need to notify immigration?
passages.text: An actual change of registered place of stay generally must be reported within 15 days, even if you stay within the same university area. Verify whether a room-only change altered the registered address.

passages.heading: Cost of Living in Korea
passages.text: Korea’s dining costs are relatively low compared to other developed countries, and public transportation costs are very affordable.

passages.heading: Essential Guide to Saving Living Expenses
passages.text:
The goal of studying abroad is not just to earn a degree but to grow through diverse experiences, making it important to save costs while having meaningful time.

- **Use Scholarships** The Korea government provides scholarships to international students annually, and students with excellent academic performance can receive university-specific scholarships.
- **Save on Housing Costs** Staying in dormitories or sharing an apartment with roommates can help reduce housing expenses.
- **Save on Food Expenses** Cook meals using groceries instead of dining out and take advantage of student discounts.
- **Save on Transportation Costs** Many cities in Korea offer bicycle rental services. Using Korea's affordable public transportation system with transfer benefits can also help save money.

passages.heading: 1) Transportation Card
passages.text:
Korea has a well-developed public transportation system including subways and
buses, allowing convenient travel between destinations throughout the country.

Public transportation fares vary depending on the mode of transportation and the
region (metropolitan or non-metropolitan areas), and using a transportation card is
cheaper than paying with cash.

Transportation Card Types

Prepaid transportation cards including T-money and Cashbee are widely used.

※ Some universities issue student ID cards that also function as debit cards with an embedded

transportation card feature.

How to Purchase and Reload Transportation Cards

• Where to purchase: Convenience stores or customer support centers within

subway stations
• How to reload: Cards can be reloaded at convenience stores, subway stations,

affiliated ATMs, or mobile apps

※ When reloading at a convenience store, check whether the store displays a transportation

card sign outside.

Notes

• Tag the card when boarding and exiting the bus or subway to pay the fare and
receive transfer discounts.

• Boarding may not be possible if the balance is low, so please check and reload the
card regularly in advance.

passages.text:

can be exchanged at banks or airport currency exchange counters. As preferential
exchange rates vary by bank, we recommend using your primary transaction bank
or select a bank offering more favorable rates. The range of currencies available for
exchange may differ by bank; therefore, it is advisable to check in advance espe-
cially when exchanging large amounts or currencies other than the US dollar (USD).

passages.heading: 1) Opening a Mobile Phone Account
passages.text:
Opening a mobile phone account facilitates everyday communication and enables
convenient access to administrative and financial services. A phone account can
be opened using an existing mobile device. If a device is not available, purchase a
mobile phone and select a service plan to open a new account.

passages.heading: Application steps
passages.text:
1. Confirm the student’s visa status, arrival date, current address, and whether their university offers group registration.
1. Reserve an immigration visit through HiKorea (www.hikorea.go.kr), unless the university has an authorized group process.
1. Prepare the integrated application form, valid passport, recent passport-style photograph, and proof of residence.
1. Prepare a certificate of enrollment or training and any visa-specific documents required by immigration.
1. Attend the appointment, submit the application, complete required biometric procedures if applicable, pay the applicable fees, and follow the collection/delivery instructions.

passages.heading: Approval Process
passages.text:
- **Step 1. Prepare an Employment Contract** Employment contract between the parties (standard employment contract, hourly wage must be stated).
- **Step 2. Prepare a Part-Time Employment Confirmation Form** Complete the designated form, signed by the university’s international student advisor.
- **Step 3. Application Submission** Submit required documents either online or in person.
- **Step 4. Approval or Rejection** Receive an approval sticker or print the permit online.

passages.heading: 가신입학
passages.text:
1) 「고등교육법 시행령」 제29조 제2항 제6호에 따른 부모 모두 외국인인 외국인

※ 우리나라 고교과정과 상응하는 교육과정을 시작하기 전 부모와 학생 모두가 외국 국적을 취득한 자 포함

2) 국내/외 고등학교 졸업(예정)자 또는 법령에 의해 동등학력이 인정된 자로, 12년 이상의 교육과정(초/중/고 정규 교육과정)을 이
수한 자

※ 단, 12년 미만의 학제를 채택하고 있는 국가에서 초·중등학교 전 교육과정을 이수한 외국인은 우리나라 고등학교 졸업자와 동

등한 학력으로 인정함

※ 초등학교 이전 기관(유아원, 유치원), 어학연수, 평생교육원 등의 교육기관 수학 연한은 인정하지 않음

※ 검정고시, 홈스쿨링, 사이버학습 등의 학력은 인정하지 않음

3) 어학능력 기준

가) 한국어 : 공인 한국어능력시험(TOPIK) 3급(PBT, IBT), SCH한국어능력시험 3급 이상, 법무부 사회통합프로그램 3단계 이상

이수, 법무부 사회통합프로그램 사전평가 61점 이상 또는 세종학당 한국어 중급1 이상(단, 온라인 세종학당 및 온라인 수강자
는 제외) 이수

passages.heading: 나. 구직비자(D-10)
passages.text:
시간제취업 위반 등 취업과 관련 최근 5년 이내 출입국관리법 위반 이력이 있는 경우
신청 대상에서 제외*
* 제외기준 : 국내체류 중 상기와 관련된 출입국관리법령 위반으로 40만원 이상의

┃제3장┃한국에서의 유학 생활

벌금, 범칙금, 과태료 처분을 받은 이력이 있는 경우
•(제도남용 방지) 무분별한 사증신청에 따른 체류질서 문란 방지차원에서 아래 경우에는
원칙적으로 사증발급 제한
- 최근 1년 이내 구직(D-10) 자격으로 6개월 이상 체류*한 적이 있는 경우
* 단, 국내 기업·단체 등의 초청을 받아 인턴사원 등으로 연수예정인 경우에는 1회에

한해 사증발급 허용(인턴 목적 D-10자격 체류는 최대 1년을 넘을 수 없음)

(4) 신청서류

75

•학위증

passages.heading: Important limitations and escalation
passages.text:
Avoid using older COVID-era re-entry restrictions as current rules. Confirm exceptions and special cases with immigration.

For immigration matters, refer students to the Immigration Contact Center (1345) for case-specific or conflicting instructions. For immediate emergencies, direct them to 112 or 119. For SCH-specific academic or housing decisions, use the current official university notice and office instructions.

passages.heading: International Students
passages.text:
91

I am currently a language trainee but plan to study
at a university. I’d like to apply for an interim visa
and I want to know the requirements.

You can apply for a visa called an interim visa if the
period between the end of your current stay and
the start of the new semester is three months or
less. To be eligible, you must meet all three of the
following requirements:

① A student in a language training program

who meets the visa extension requirements,
including attendance rate;

② A student who has successfully completed

the language training program and who has
been admitted to a degree program equivalent
to an associate degree or higher at the same
university. If the student is admitted to a
different university, the new school must be a
general university or higher;

③ A student with TOPIK score of Level 3 or higher,

or a student who has stayed in Korea for 18
months or longer with a Language Student visa
and with proven Korean language proficiency.

I have applied for foreign resident registration, but I
moved to my friend’s home and my home address
has changed. What should I do?

If your home address has changed, you must
report the change of residence within 15 days. If
you did not sign the residence contract yourself
and you are staying at a provided residence
instead, you must submit (1) the lease agreement,
(2) a confirmation letter stating that the residence
is being provided, and (3) a copy of the residence
provider’s (friend’s) ID card.

passages.heading: ★ 입학서류 제출 관련 유의사항 ★
passages.text:
가. 모든 입학서류(신분증, 여권 등 일부 서류 제외)는 한글 또는 영문으로 작성된 원본을 제출해야함
※ 서류의 원본이 한글 또는 영문이 아닐 시 한글 또는 영문 번역본을 첨부하여 제출
나. 서류가 원본이 아닐 시 사본을 공증 받아 제출해야함
다. 상기 입학서류는 대학 제출용이며, 재외 공관 및 출입국관리사무소에 제출하는 서류는 별도로 준비해야함
라. 입학서류는 지원자의 조건에 따라 일부 상이할 수 있음
마. 일정을 준수하여 서류를 제출해야 하며, 제출기한을 초과할 경우 인정하지 않음
바. 서류검토 결과 그 내용이 사실과 다르거나 오류가 있을 시 인정하지 않음
사. 제출된 서류는 반환하지 않음. 단, 1차 모집 지원자가 불합격 후 다음 차수 모집에 지원할 경우, 대학입학지원자격심사신청서

passages.heading: (2) Understanding Programs
passages.text:
Korean Language Program

The Korean Language Program is an intensive course designed to help international
students improve their Korean language skills, which are essential for pursuing
degree programs or for daily life in Korea.
The program is generally offered by university-affiliated Korean language institutes,
and students are required to obtain a Korean Language Trainee (D-4-1) Visa.

6

University-Affiliated Korean Language Institutes
The institutes offer structured programs in speaking, listening, reading, and
writing to meet various needs such as university admission, job hunting, TOPIK
preparation, and business communication.

- Program Overview (Example)

※ Course details may vary depending on the language institute, so please check the

website of your chosen institute for the most accurate information.

<Regular Courses>
✓ Operation Period: Four semesters per year (Spring, Summer, Fall, Winter)

10 weeks per semester (within 200 Hours), 5 days a week (Monday–
Friday)

✓ Levels: Stage 1 (Beginner) – Stage 6 (Advanced). Students are placed by

their language proficiency.

✓ Course Structure: Listening, speaking, reading, and writing

✓ Evaluation Method: Based on attendance, tests, and homework

assignments.

✓ Completion Requirements: Students will receive a certificate of

completion upon meeting the required attendance and grade standards.
They may then advance to higher-level classes.

<Special or Short-term Courses>
In addition to regular courses, the institutes also offer various special or
short-term programs based on students’ needs.

✓ TOPIK Preparation Course: An intensive program designed to prepare

students for the TOPIK exam. It focuses on problem-solving practice
using actual past test questions.

✓ College Admission Course: Customized curriculum for Korean university

passages.heading: Korean Language Training Programs
passages.text:
Korean language training programs are designed for foreigners and aim to teach the Korean language. These programs are generally divided into long-term courses lasting 10 weeks or more, and short-term courses lasting 4 weeks or less. Students can choose the program that best suits their needs and apply accordingly.

Source : https://easylaw.go.kr/ Ministry of Legislation

passages.heading: Regular Programs
passages.text:
"Regular programs" refer to academic courses identical to those typically undertaken by Korean students. Admission to a regular program is available to those who meet the previously mentioned admission requirements (completion of the prior stage of education, possession of equivalent academic qualifications as recognized by law, and fulfillment of the school’s admission criteria). Example : To enter a university in Korea, applicants must have graduated from high school or hold an equivalent level of education as recognized by Korean law.

※ Not all regular programs are open to international students. Broadcast universities, correspondence universities, broadcast and correspondence universities, and cyber universities, which are established as distance learning institutions, do not permit international students to enroll.

passages.heading: Short-Term Programs
passages.text: "Short-term programs" refer to completing only part of a regular program, typically over one or two semesters, or during seasonal sessions held during vacation periods. Short-term programs are often pursued through exchange arrangements, rather than direct applications to the host school. These arrangements are made between the home school (the school the student is attending in their home country) and a domestic school in Korea with an academic exchange agreement (hereinafter referred to as “partner schools”). Schools with academic exchange agreements often provide benefits such as simplified admission processes, credit transfer, and scholarships. Students interested in short-term programs should check whether their home school has a partner school in Korea.

passages.heading: Permissible Scope
passages.text:
Individuals with a certain level of Korean language proficiency, as verified by the university’s international student advisor.

- Holders of study stay statuses D-2-1 to D-2-4, D-2-6, and D-2-7.
- Language training (D-4-1, D-4-7) or visiting student (D-2-8) status holders after 6 months from the qualification change date (or entry date for visa holders).

passages.heading: Regular Programs
passages.text:
"Regular programs" refer to academic courses identical to those typically undertaken by Korean students. Admission to a regular program is available to those who meet the previously mentioned admission requirements (completion of the prior stage of education, possession of equivalent academic qualifications as recognized by law, and fulfillment of the school’s admission criteria). Example : To enter a university in Korea, applicants must have graduated from high school or hold an equivalent level of education as recognized by Korean law.

※ Not all regular programs are open to international students. Broadcast universities, correspondence universities, broadcast and correspondence universities, and cyber universities, which are established as distance learning institutions, do not permit international students to enroll.

passages.heading: Korean Language Training Programs
passages.text:
Korean language training programs are designed for foreigners and aim to teach the Korean language. These programs are generally divided into long-term courses lasting 10 weeks or more, and short-term courses lasting 4 weeks or less. Students can choose the program that best suits their needs and apply accordingly.

Source : https://easylaw.go.kr/ Ministry of Legislation

passages.heading: Short-Term Programs
passages.text: "Short-term programs" refer to completing only part of a regular program, typically over one or two semesters, or during seasonal sessions held during vacation periods. Short-term programs are often pursued through exchange arrangements, rather than direct applications to the host school. These arrangements are made between the home school (the school the student is attending in their home country) and a domestic school in Korea with an academic exchange agreement (hereinafter referred to as “partner schools”). Schools with academic exchange agreements often provide benefits such as simplified admission processes, credit transfer, and scholarships. Students interested in short-term programs should check whether their home school has a partner school in Korea.

passages.heading: FAQ 5. I moved to a new dormitory. Do I need to notify immigration?
passages.text: An actual change of registered place of stay generally must be reported within 15 days, even if you stay within the same university area. Verify whether a room-only change altered the registered address.

passages.heading: Dormitory to dormitory or dormitory to apartment
passages.text: If the registered residential address changes, report it even if you are staying at the same university. Check with your dormitory administration for a residence certificate. The university also may require a separate profile-address update.

passages.heading: 3) Visiting Healthcare Providers
passages.text:
Mandatory ID check

Pursuant to the National Health Insurance Act, individuals visiting a healthcare
provider must verify their identity by presenting a valid ID card before receiving
medical services. Medical services cannot be provided without presenting an ID
card. Acceptable forms of identification include those with a photo and a foreign
resident registration number, such as a residence card, passport,
or driver's license issued in Korea. A mobile health insurance
card can also be used in place of a physical ID card.

passages.heading: International Students
passages.text:
89

I left the country after submitting a civil petition
to the immigration office. Can the office review
the matter while I’m overseas or handle it after I
reenter the country?

If an applicant is confirmed to have left the country
during the review process, the review will be
suspended or may be terminated at the discretion
of the immigration officer.

This is because the inquiry cannot remain unre-
solved for an extended period when it is uncertain
whether the applicant will return to the country,
and it is difficult to obtain additional information
when further confirmation is needed during the
review. Therefore, please make your inquiry with
your departure schedule in mind. In unavoidable
circumstances, you should submit the inquiry
again after reentering the country.

I plan to return to my home country after gradua-
tion, and this will terminate my visa. Is there a way
to get employed after I return to Korea?

We recommend obtaining approval for a visa
change before leaving the country if you plan to
look for a job after graduation or if your employ-
ment has already been confirmed.

If you do not have enough time, you may apply for
a Job Seeker (D-10) visa after leaving the country.
If this is your first Job Seeker (D-10) visa after
graduation and it is within one year of your grad-
uation date, you will be exempted from the point-
based system.

is the maximum permitted period of stay—while
completing my bachelor’s degree program at a
university. However, I still need to have my thesis
reviewed. Can I extend my period of stay?

passages.heading: 3) Visiting Healthcare Providers
passages.text:
Mandatory ID check

Pursuant to the National Health Insurance Act, individuals visiting a healthcare
provider must verify their identity by presenting a valid ID card before receiving
medical services. Medical services cannot be provided without presenting an ID
card. Acceptable forms of identification include those with a photo and a foreign
resident registration number, such as a residence card, passport,
or driver's license issued in Korea. A mobile health insurance
card can also be used in place of a physical ID card.
